# Tally spike findings

Lane A (session neatlogs-hack-2). Commands were run on this machine on 10 Oct 2026. Updated as spikes finish.

## S1

**Answer:** Yes. A script can spawn an AO worker with a chosen model and harness, read its status, and kill it. It cannot read the worker's result; judge by branch/PR and our own test run.

**Evidence:**

S1 AO spawn/read/kill: YES, fully scriptable.
- Spawn: `ao spawn --project neatlogs-hack --harness claude-code --model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 --name tally-spike-s1-haiku --prompt "...Reply PONG..."` -> `spawned session neatlogs-hack-3 "tally-spike-s1-haiku" (idle)`. Same with `--harness codex --model gpt-5.6-luna` -> neatlogs-hack-4. `ao spawn` has no --json; the id must be parsed from that line.
- Status: `ao session get <id> --json` -> {session:{id,harness,status,activity:{state,lastActivityAt},isTerminated,branch,branchState:{commits,unpushed},prs:[]}}. Observed status "working"/activity "active" then "idle"/"idle" ~13 s after spawn (Haiku) and ~19 s (Codex). `ao session ls --json -p neatlogs-hack --include-terminated` lists them (orchestrators only with -a). GET http://127.0.0.1:3001/api/v1/sessions/<id> also returns `model`.
- Result: there is NO transcript/output endpoint (GET /api/v1/sessions/<id>/messages|transcript|output|events all 404). "idle" only means the turn ended, not that the task succeeded. Tally must judge by branch/PR + its own test run (as planned). The Haiku reply "PONG" was confirmed only by reading the Claude transcript file under ~/.claude/projects/<worktree-path>/.
- Kill: `ao session kill neatlogs-hack-3` -> "session neatlogs-hack-3 killed", then status "terminated", isTerminated true. Both test sessions are killed.
- Bad model is rejected up front: `--model not-a-real-model` -> "model ... is not in the active provider catalog (UNSUPPORTED_MODEL)".
- Model ids, from GET /api/v1/agents/<harness>/models. claude-code: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 (cheap), claude-haiku-5-5, claude-sonnet-5-5 (middle), claude-sonnet-5, claude-sonnet-4-6, claude-opus-5-5 (top), claude-opus-5, claude-opus-4-8/4-7/4-6, claude-fable-5, claude-fable-5-1, alias `opus`. codex: gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-6-luna (cheap), gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-6-astra (middle), gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-6-sol, gpt-6.1-sol (top; default). Which codex id is which tier is my reading of the names, not something AO states.

**Still unverified:** Tier order of the Codex model ids is inferred from their names. How AO behaves when a subscription usage limit is hit mid-run.

## S2

**Answer:** Tokens yes. Estimated cost is reliable for Codex and unreliable for Claude Code, so Tally must compute cost as tokens x list price.

**Evidence:**

S2 usage endpoint shape (GET /api/v1/usage/sessions/{id}):
{sessionId, incomplete, totals:{inputTokens, cachedInputTokens, uncachedInputTokens, outputTokens, processedTokens, cacheReadTokens, estimatedCost}, harnesses:[{harness, totals, models:[{modelId, totals}]}]}. estimatedCost = null or {totalNanos, inputNanos, cachedInputNanos, outputNanos, coverage:"complete"|"partial", providerAttribution:"observed"}; unit is nanos of USD (1e9 = $1). List form /api/v1/usage/sessions -> {sessions:[{sessionId, processedTokens, totalTokens, incomplete, estimatedCost}]}.
- inputTokens includes cached; Claude cache-WRITE tokens are folded into uncachedInputTokens (Haiku test: 10 input + 16,874 cache-creation in the transcript = 16,884 uncached in AO). AO does not expose cache writes separately.
- Codex: estimatedCost populated within ~10 s (gpt-5.6-luna test: 21,606 tokens -> totalNanos 2,345,760 = $0.0023; implies $0.20/M input, $0.02/M cached, $1.20/M output).
- Claude Code: NOT reliable. Haiku session: estimatedCost null (tokens present). Across all sessions on this daemon: claude-opus-5-5 has cost on 17 sessions and null on 1 (this live session, still null at 660k tokens); claude-haiku-4-5 null on its only session. Also all totals were null for the first ~30-40 s of the Haiku session.
- Consequence: the watcher can poll tokens, but Tally must compute cost itself as tokens x list price from tally.yaml and treat AO's estimatedCost as optional. Ceilings cannot fire in the first ~30 s of a worker.

**Still unverified:** Why some Claude Code sessions get an estimate and others do not. Whether cache-write tokens can be separated (AO folds them into uncached input; Entire does report them separately).

## S3

**Answer:** Sending works from TypeScript with the key we have. Listing past traces does not: it needs a service-account token and project id that we do not have.

**Evidence:**

S3 neatlogs:
- Read API exists: https://app.neatlogs.com/api/v1/public/... (GET /traces with from/to/status/workflowName/sessionId filters returning totalCostUsd, totalTokens, status, durationMs per trace; GET /traces/{id}, /traces/{id}/spans; POST /analytics/cost, /analytics/kpis, /analytics/export). It needs a service-account token (Settings -> Service Accounts, scopes context:read + observability:read) sent as `Authorization: Bearer` plus `x-project-id`.
- NEATLOGS_API_KEY is an ingest key and is refused there: GET /api/v1/public/traces?limit=3 with it as x-api-key and as Bearer -> 401 "A valid public API credential is required." So listing past runs is NOT possible with what we have. Needed from the human: a service-account token + project UUID (suggest NEATLOGS_TOKEN and NEATLOGS_PROJECT_ID in ~/.tally/.env). Until then use the plan's fallback (Tally's own history file).
- Single-trace readback DOES work with the ingest key on an undocumented path the SDK's own doctor uses: GET https://ingest.neatlogs.com/api/traces/v3/{traceId} with x-api-key -> 200 with name, workflowName, sessionId, status, spanCount, totalTokensUsed, totalTokensCost, spans[]. Verified on a trace I sent. Undocumented, so do not build on it beyond verification.
- (a) Send from our TypeScript: `npm install neatlogs` (1.1.28, Node >=18). `await init({apiKey, workflowName, tags})`, then `await trace({name, kind:'CHAIN', sessionId, input}, async () => ...)`, `await flush(); await shutdown()`. Trace id is available inside the callback via `injectTraceContext(carrier)` (W3C traceparent). `sessionId` goes on trace(), not init() (init rejects it: UNKNOWN_INIT_OPTION). `npm exec -- neatlogs doctor --probe --json` with our key -> status "pass", all 17 checks pass incl. TRACE_VISIBLE and TRACE_FINALIZED. No LLM client wrapper is needed for the CFO agent's decisions; manual spans are enough.
- (b) Worker sessions: `npm i -g @neatlogs/claude-code && neatlogs-claude-code setup --global --api-key KEY` (hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json, one trace per session) and `npm i -g @neatlogs/codex && neatlogs-codex setup --global --api-key KEY` (hooks in ~/.codex/hooks.json, one trace per user prompt; needs the hooks trusted once via /hooks in Codex). Both also read NEATLOGS_API_KEY from env. Neither is installed yet (`which` finds neither); I did not install them because --global edits the human's ~/.claude and ~/.codex settings. Could not verify how a worker trace is tied to a Tally task id, or the dashboard URL format for a trace link.

**Still unverified:** Dashboard URL format for a trace link. How a worker session trace is tied to a Tally task id. The hook packages for Claude Code and Codex are documented but were not installed or run.

## S4

**Answer:** Yes. Entire is enabled; entire-graph (a separate plugin) gives usable search and impact numbers on a fresh clone in seconds.

**Evidence:**

S4 Entire + entire-graph: YES.
- `entire enable --agent claude-code --telemetry=false` then `entire agent add codex` -> "Installed 9 hooks for Claude Code", "Installed 7 hooks for Codex". Added .claude/settings.json, .codex/hooks.json, .entire/settings.json, .entire/.gitignore; committed as 3ec86ac. Warning printed: Codex reads hooks from the ROOT checkout (/Users/vaibhaav/Downloads/neatlogs-hack/.codex/hooks.json), so Codex capture is inactive in worktrees until this commit reaches the default branch.
- Graph is a plugin, not present by default: `entire plugin install graph` -> v0.4.0. I did not run `entire graph init-agents` here (it would add AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md).
- On a fresh clone of fly-doom-jev: `entire graph index --repo .` -> 3.0 s, files 110, parsed 108, symbols 1042, relations 3640 (CALLS 878, IMPORTS 486, FILE_CHANGES_WITH 338), Python 64 files. `entire graph search --repo . --profile full --format json --query "<issue text>"` returns ranked results with file_path, symbol, qualified_name, signals. `entire graph impact --repo . --symbol LiveLoop.request_new_episode --format json` -> callers{total 2,direct 1,transitive 1}, callees{0}, type_consumers{0}, data_flows{0}, co_changes{total 22}, siblings{9}; ~0.6 s on cache hit. No network, repo left clean.
- Sizing recipe that works from the CLI: search on the issue text -> take top symbols -> impact on each -> count distinct files, callers and co-change files. Impact takes a symbol, not an issue, so the search step is required. Also found: `entire graph verify --test "<cmd>" --record-baseline/--pre-edit-baseline` reports which tests newly pass/fail vs a baseline (pytest and vitest parsers); useful for lane B's verifier. Not tried.

**Still unverified:** `entire graph verify` (test verdict vs a baseline) was not tried. Quality of sizing from search + impact on real issue text.

## S5

**Answer:** Yes across model and harness, by passing the checkpoint summary as text to a new session. `entire session resume` is not usable for this.

**Evidence:**

S5 Handoff across model and harness: YES via summary text; `entire session resume` is not the right tool.
- The session-handoff skill (github.com/entireio/skills) is just instructions run by the RECEIVING agent: `entire session list --json` -> `entire session info <id> --transcript` -> summarise -> continue. For a checkpoint: `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json|--transcript`. Nothing in it is model- or harness-specific.
- Test in a scratch repo: ran `claude -p --model claude-haiku-4-5-20251001` (left a bug unfixed on purpose). `entire session list --json` showed it: agent "Claude Code", turns 1, tokens {input 26, cache_read 60136, cache_write 13879, output 763}. After a commit: trailer `Entire-Checkpoint: 01M4JS7CY6YKM1QR9BC776KVYK`; `entire checkpoint explain <id> --json` gives model, files_touched, token_usage (with cache_creation_tokens split out, which AO lacks); `--transcript` streamed 54 lines / 262 KB. `entire checkpoint explain --generate <id>` wrote an Intent/Outcome summary in 8 s (it calls Claude Code "sonnet" itself: spend outside the ledger).
- Passed that summary as the prompt to `codex exec -m gpt-5.6-luna -s workspace-write`: Codex fixed the bug in 28 s (13,265 tokens), calc.py now returns a + b. So Claude Code -> Codex handoff works with summary + same branch.
- `entire session resume <branch>` restores the SAME agent's session log and prints that agent's resume command; it asks interactive questions and can reset git state. Not usable for a different harness. Recommendation: escalation = new AO worker on the failed branch with the `checkpoint explain` summary in its prompt.
- Could not verify: the Codex exec run printed "hook: Stop Completed" but did not appear in `entire session list` afterwards.

**Still unverified:** Whether Entire captures headless `codex exec` sessions (the run did not appear in `entire session list`). Handoff on a large, long session. `--generate` spends Claude tokens outside the ledger.

## S6

**Answer:** Skipped: the cfoai MCP server is not connected.

**Evidence:**

S6 cfo.ai: SKIPPED. `claude mcp list` -> "cfoai: https://api.cfo.ai/mcp (HTTP) - ! Needs authentication". The human must approve it in a browser; CSV fallback stands until then.

**Still unverified:** Everything. Needs the human to approve the MCP server in a browser.

## S7 LLM gateway models

**Answer:** Claude Code can drive all seven gateway models, Claude and Nova, when run directly against the gateway. Running it as an AO worker is BLOCKED on one decision: AO only accepts a gateway worker if the key itself is stored in the AO project's env. Codex and OpenCode 2 could not drive Nova on this gateway. Gateway budget is 20 USD per 30 days; 0.04 USD spent by these tests.

**Evidence:**

Gateway (LiteLLM, key read from ~/.tally/.env, never printed):
- `GET /v1/models` -> 200: nova-micro, nova-lite, nova-pro, nova-2-lite, claude-haiku, claude-sonnet-4.6, claude-opus-4.6.
- `GET /key/info` -> 200: spend 0.0 (before tests), max_budget 20.0, budget_duration 30d, budget_reset_at 2026-11-01, rpm_limit 60, tpm_limit none. After all tests: spend 0.0402. The figure lags a request by 10-15 s.
- `GET /spend/logs` -> 401 "Only proxy admin". So the gateway gives this key a running total only, no per-request or per-session breakdown.
- All three wire formats answer: `POST /v1/chat/completions` (nova-micro, 200, usage with prompt/completion tokens), `POST /v1/messages` (claude-haiku 200; nova-micro also 200 in Anthropic format), `POST /v1/responses` (nova-micro 200).

Claude Code, run directly (`claude -p`) with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=<gateway host, no /v1>` and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<key>`:
- `--model claude-haiku`: replied PONG. usage: input 10, cache_creation 28,087, output 254. Prompt caching works for Claude through the gateway.
- `--model nova-lite`: first try failed with "maximum tokens you requested exceeds the model limit of 10000". With `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8000` it read calc.py, fixed the bug and saved the file in 3 turns (49,179 input tokens, 225 output, no caching).
- The key can stay out of the environment: `--settings '{"apiKeyHelper":"<script that prints the key from ~/.tally/.env>"}'` with only `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` set also worked (nova-micro replied PONG).
- Claude Code's own `total_cost_usd` is wrong for gateway model ids (it logs `unrecognized_model` and reported 0.1456 USD for a call the gateway charged about 0.036 for, and 0.20 USD for the nova-lite run). Do not use it.

Other harnesses with Nova:
- Codex with a custom provider (`-c model_providers.x.base_url=... wire_api="responses"`): nova-lite -> 400 "The provided request is not valid"; nova-2-lite -> 403 "not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeTool". `wire_api="chat"` is no longer accepted by this Codex build. Not usable.
- OpenCode 2 (v2.0.21) with an `opencode.json` openai-compatible provider: "Route.model(openai-compatible-chat) requires an endpoint baseURL". Its config format differs from OpenCode 1; not pursued. aider is not installed.

AO pass-through (throwaway AO project `gw-spike` on a scratch repo; the neatlogs-hack project config was not touched):
- `ao spawn` has no env flag. Env is per PROJECT: `ao project set-config <id> --env KEY=VALUE` (it replaces the whole config) and `--post-create <cmd>` runs in each new worktree.
- With `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` in project env, every `--model` value is rejected, including catalogue ids: `model capabilities unavailable for model "claude-haiku": catalog is stale (MODEL_CAPABILITIES_UNAVAILABLE)`. The model has to come from project env (`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`), so one AO project can serve one gateway model.
- With the model in env and the key supplied only through apiKeyHelper (written by post-create), spawn is refused: chat mode -> `agent requires authentication (CHAT_DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE)`; `--mode tui` -> `The agent is installed but the project credential was rejected (AGENT_AUTH_REQUIRED)`; same with `--skip-agent-check`.
- So AO wants the credential in the project env. I did not put the key there: that copies the secret into AO's config store, which the rules forbid without a decision.

Prices, USD per million tokens (input / output / cache read). Source: the gateway's own `GET /model/info`, which is what this key is charged.

| Gateway id | Underlying Bedrock model | Input | Output | Cache read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nova-micro | us.amazon.nova-micro-v1:0 | 0.035 | 0.14 | 0.00875 |
| nova-lite | us.amazon.nova-lite-v1:0 | 0.06 | 0.24 | 0.015 |
| nova-2-lite | us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 | 0.33 | 2.75 | 0.0825 |
| nova-pro | us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0 | 0.80 | 3.20 | 0.20 |
| claude-haiku | us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 | 1.10 | 5.50 | 0.11 |
| claude-sonnet-4.6 | us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 | 3.30 | 16.50 | 0.33 |
| claude-opus-4.6 | us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1 | 5.50 | 27.50 | 0.55 |

The three Claude rates are exactly 10% above Anthropic's first-party list (Haiku 4.5 1/5, Sonnet 4.6 3/15, Opus 4.6 5/25, from Anthropic's model table). Use the gateway rates in tally.yaml for gateway tiers, since that is what is billed.

Schema: tiers now carry a required `provider` string (commit 3dae374, pushed). A tier is {name, harness, model, provider, price{input, cachedInput, output per MTok}, ceilingFraction}.

**Still unverified:**
- Whether AO's usage endpoint reports tokens and cost for a gateway worker. No gateway worker could be spawned. Expect tokens to appear (AO read them for subscription sessions) and cost to be null for unknown model ids; this is a guess.
- The AWS public price page did not render the Nova or current Claude rows when fetched, so the Nova list prices are confirmed only against the gateway.
- Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6 through Claude Code (only claude-haiku was run; same path, higher cost).
- Nova on a real multi-file task. No prompt caching was seen for Nova, so long sessions resend the full context each turn.

**Decision needed:** may the gateway key be stored in an AO project's env (`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`)? If yes, the working shape is one AO project per gateway tier (env: base URL, token, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8000` for Nova). If no, the alternative is a small local proxy run by Tally that holds the key and forwards to the gateway, with a dummy token in AO; that would also let Tally meter and cap spend per worker itself.

## fly-doom-jev test check

**Answer:** The suite passes in a fresh clone; every test file is fast and self-contained enough to be a pass/fail check.

**Evidence:**

- Fresh clone at f99b54c in ~/tally-scratch. Nothing was changed on GitHub.
- `make setup` -> 54 s (uv venv with Python 3.14.8, `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"`).
- `make test` -> `90 passed in 7.53s` (8.9 s wall) on the first run, `90 passed in 1.02s` on the second. 0 skipped. README says 89.
- Needs: uv, Python 3.14 (pyproject allows >=3.12), Apple clang. The C kernel builds itself on the first test run into engine/native/build (gitignored). No network, no API key (Jev is mocked), no data download: the 231 MB processed connectome is committed.
- Costs: clone took about 12 minutes (311 MB pack, 695 MB on disk). .venv is 453 MB and every worker worktree needs its own `make setup`. Working tree stays clean after tests.
- Per file, run alone (all under 0.5 s): test_bridge_guard 4, test_decoder 7, test_engine 3, test_full_connectome 6, test_graph 5, test_hf_export 1, test_jev 10, test_jev_live 14, test_plasticity 12, test_recording 2, test_reflexes 10, test_state_encoder 3, test_viz_export 3, test_weighting 9 (tests/unit), test_closed_loop 1 (tests/integration).

**Still unverified:** `make setup` inside an AO worker worktree (expected to work; not run). Behaviour on Linux or without clang.

## S3

**Still unverified:** Dashboard URL format for a trace link. How a worker session trace is tied to a Tally task id. The hook packages for Claude Code and Codex are documented but were not installed or run.

## S4

**Answer:** Yes. Entire is enabled; entire-graph (a separate plugin) gives usable search and impact numbers on a fresh clone in seconds.

**Evidence:**

## S5

**Answer:** Yes across model and harness, by passing the checkpoint summary as text to a new session. `entire session resume` is not usable for this.

**Evidence:**

S5 Handoff across model and harness: YES via summary text; `entire session resume` is not the right tool.

## S6

**Answer:** Skipped: the cfoai MCP server is not connected.

**Evidence:**

S6 cfo.ai: SKIPPED. `claude mcp list` -> "cfoai: https://api.cfo.ai/mcp (HTTP) - ! Needs authentication". The human must approve it in a browser; CSV fallback stands until then.

**Still unverified:** Everything. Needs the human to approve the MCP server in a browser.

## S7 LLM gateway models

**Answer:** Claude Code can drive all seven gateway models, Claude and Nova, when run directly against the gateway. Running it as an AO worker is BLOCKED on one decision: AO only accepts a gateway worker if the key itself is stored in the AO project's env. Codex and OpenCode 2 could not drive Nova on this gateway. Gateway budget is 20 USD per 30 days; 0.04 USD spent by these tests.

**Evidence:**

Gateway (LiteLLM, key read from ~/.tally/.env, never printed):
- `GET /v1/models` -> 200: nova-micro, nova-lite, nova-pro, nova-2-lite, claude-haiku, claude-sonnet-4.6, claude-opus-4.6.
- `GET /key/info` -> 200: spend 0.0 (before tests), max_budget 20.0, budget_duration 30d, budget_reset_at 2026-11-01, rpm_limit 60, tpm_limit none. After all tests: spend 0.0402. The figure lags a request by 10-15 s.
- `GET /spend/logs` -> 401 "Only proxy admin". So the gateway gives this key a running total only, no per-request or per-session breakdown.
- All three wire formats answer: `POST /v1/chat/completions` (nova-micro, 200, usage with prompt/completion tokens), `POST /v1/messages` (claude-haiku 200; nova-micro also 200 in Anthropic format), `POST /v1/responses` (nova-micro 200).

Claude Code, run directly (`claude -p`) with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=<gateway host, no /v1>` and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<key>`:
- `--model claude-haiku`: replied PONG. usage: input 10, cache_creation 28,087, output 254. Prompt caching works for Claude through the gateway.
- `--model nova-lite`: first try failed with "maximum tokens you requested exceeds the model limit of 10000". With `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8000` it read calc.py, fixed the bug and saved the file in 3 turns (49,179 input tokens, 225 output, no caching).
- The key can stay out of the environment: `--settings '{"apiKeyHelper":"<script that prints the key from ~/.tally/.env>"}'` with only `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` set also worked (nova-micro replied PONG).
- Claude Code's own `total_cost_usd` is wrong for gateway model ids (it logs `unrecognized_model` and reported 0.1456 USD for a call the gateway charged about 0.036 for, and 0.20 USD for the nova-lite run). Do not use it.

Other harnesses with Nova:
- Codex with a custom provider (`-c model_providers.x.base_url=... wire_api="responses"`): nova-lite -> 400 "The provided request is not valid"; nova-2-lite -> 403 "not authorized to perform: bedrock:InvokeTool". `wire_api="chat"` is no longer accepted by this Codex build. Not usable.
- OpenCode 2 (v2.0.21) with an `opencode.json` openai-compatible provider: "Route.model(openai-compatible-chat) requires an endpoint baseURL". Its config format differs from OpenCode 1; not pursued. aider is not installed.

AO pass-through (throwaway AO project `gw-spike` on a scratch repo; the neatlogs-hack project config was not touched):
- `ao spawn` has no env flag. Env is per PROJECT: `ao project set-config <id> --env KEY=VALUE` (it replaces the whole config) and `--post-create <cmd>` runs in each new worktree.
- With `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` in project env, every `--model` value is rejected, including catalogue ids: `model capabilities unavailable for model "claude-haiku": catalog is stale (MODEL_CAPABILITIES_UNAVAILABLE)`. The model has to come from project env (`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`), so one AO project can serve one gateway model.
- With the model in env and the key supplied only through apiKeyHelper (written by post-create), spawn is refused: chat mode -> `agent requires authentication (CHAT_DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE)`; `--mode tui` -> `The agent is installed but the project credential was rejected (AGENT_AUTH_REQUIRED)`; same with `--skip-agent-check`.
- So AO wants the credential in the project env. I did not put the key there: that copies the secret into AO's config store, which the rules forbid without a decision.

Prices, USD per million tokens (input / output / cache read). Source: the gateway's own `GET /model/info`, which is what this key is charged.

| Gateway id | Underlying Bedrock model | Input | Output | Cache read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nova-micro | us.amazon.nova-micro-v1:0 | 0.035 | 0.14 | 0.00875 |
| nova-lite | us.amazon.nova-lite-v1:0 | 0.06 | 0.24 | 0.015 |
| nova-2-lite | us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 | 0.33 | 2.75 | 0.0825 |
| nova-pro | us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0 | 0.80 | 3.20 | 0.20 |
| claude-haiku | us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 | 1.10 | 5.50 | 0.11 |
| claude-sonnet-4.6 | us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 | 3.30 | 16.50 | 0.33 |
| claude-opus-4.6 | us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1 | 5.50 | 27.50 | 0.55 |

The three Claude rates are exactly 10% above Anthropic's first-party list (Haiku 4.5 1/5, Sonnet 4.6 3/15, Opus 4.6 5/25, from Anthropic's model table). Use the gateway rates in tally.yaml for gateway tiers, since that is what is billed.

Schema: tiers now carry a required `provider` string (commit 3dae374, pushed). A tier is {name, harness, model, provider, price{input, cachedInput, output per MTok}, ceilingFraction}.

**Still unverified:**
- Whether AO's usage endpoint reports tokens and cost for a gateway worker. No gateway worker could be spawned. Expect tokens to appear (AO read them for subscription sessions) and cost to be null for unknown model ids; this is a guess.
- The AWS public price page did not render the Nova or current Claude rows when fetched, so the Nova list prices are confirmed only against the gateway.
- Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6 through Claude Code (only claude-haiku was run; same path, higher cost).
- Nova on a real multi-file task. No prompt caching was seen for Nova, so long sessions resend the full context each turn.

**Decision needed:** may the gateway key be stored in an AO project's env (`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`)? If yes, the working shape is one AO project per gateway tier (env: base URL, token, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8000` for Nova). If no, the alternative is a small local proxy run by Tally that holds the key and forwards to the gateway, with a dummy token in AO; that would also let Tally meter and cap spend per worker itself.

## fly-doom-jev test check

**Answer:** The suite passes in a fresh clone; every test file is fast and self-contained enough to be a pass/fail check.

**Evidence:**

- Fresh clone at f99b54c in ~/tally-scratch. Nothing was changed on GitHub.
- `make setup` -> 54 s (uv venv with Python 3.14.8, `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"`).
- `make test` -> `90 passed in 7.53s` (8.9 s wall) on the first run, `90 passed in 1.02s` on the second. 0 skipped. README says 89.
- Needs: uv, Python 3.14 (pyproject allows >=3.12), Apple clang. The C kernel builds itself on the first test run into engine/native/build (gitignored). No network, no API key (Jev is mocked), no data download: the 231 MB processed connectome is committed.
- Costs: clone took about 12 minutes (311 MB pack, 695 MB on disk). .venv is 453 MB and every worker worktree needs its own `make setup`. Working tree stays clean after tests.
- Per file, run alone (all under 0.5 s): test_bridge_guard 4, test_decoder 7, test_engine 3, test_full_connectome 6, test_graph 5, test_hf_export 1, test_jev 10, test_jev_live 14, test_plasticity 12, test_recording 2, test_reflexes 10, test_state_encoder 3, test_viz_export 3, test_weighting 9 (tests/unit), test_closed_loop 1 (tests/integration).

**Still unverified:** `make setup` inside an AO worker worktree (expected to work; not run). Behaviour on Linux or without clang.

## S7 LLM gateway models

**Answer:** Claude Code can drive all seven gateway models, Claude and Nova, when run directly against the gateway. Running it as an AO worker is BLOCKED on one decision: AO only accepts a gateway worker if the key itself is stored in the AO project's env. Codex and OpenCode 2 could not drive Nova on this gateway. Gateway budget is 20 USD per 30 days; 0.04 USD spent by these tests.

**Evidence:**

Gateway (LiteLLM, key read from ~/.tally/.env, never printed):
- `GET /v1/models` -> 200: nova-micro, nova-lite, nova-pro, nova-2-lite, claude-haiku, claude-sonnet-4.6, claude-opus-4.6.
- `GET /key/info` -> 200: spend 0.0 (before tests), max_budget 20.0, budget_duration 30d, budget_reset_at 2026-11-01, rpm_limit 60, tpm_limit none. After all tests: spend 0.0402. The figure lags a request by 10-15 s.
- `GET /spend/logs` -> 401 "Only proxy admin". So the gateway gives this key a running total only, no per-request or per-session breakdown.
- All three wire formats answer: `POST /v1/chat/completions` (nova-micro, 200, usage with prompt/completion tokens), `POST /v1/messages` (claude-haiku 200; nova-micro also 200 in Anthropic format), `POST /v1/responses` (nova-micro 200).

Claude Code, run directly (`claude -p`) with `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=<gateway host, no /v1>` and `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN=<key>`:
- `--model claude-haiku`: replied PONG. usage: input 10, cache_creation 28,087, output 254. Prompt caching works for Claude through the gateway.
- `--model nova-lite`: first try failed with "maximum tokens you requested exceeds the model limit of 10000". With `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8000` it read calc.py, fixed the bug and saved the file in 3 turns (49,179 input tokens, 225 output, no caching).
- The key can stay out of the environment: `--settings '{"apiKeyHelper":"<script that prints the key from ~/.tally/.env>"}'` with only `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` set also worked (nova-micro replied PONG).

The model has to come from project env (`ANTHROPIC_MODEL`), so one AO project can serve one gateway model.
- With the model in env and the key supplied only through apiKeyHelper (written by post-create), spawn is refused: chat mode -> `agent requires authentication (CHAT_DRIVER_UNAVAILABLE)`; `--mode tui` -> `The agent is installed but the project credential was rejected (AGENT_AUTH_REQUIRED)`; same with `--skip-agent-check`.
- So AO wants the credential in the project env. I did not put the key there: that copies the secret into AO's config store, which the rules forbid without a decision.

Prices, USD per million tokens (input / output / cache read). Source: the gateway's own `GET /model/info`, which is what this key is charged.

| Gateway id | Underlying Bedrock model | Input | Output | Cache read |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| nova-micro | us.amazon.nova-micro-v1:0 | 0.035 | 0.14 | 0.00875 |
| nova-lite | us.amazon.nova-lite-v1:0 | 0.06 | 0.24 | 0.015 |
| nova-2-lite | us.amazon.nova-2-lite-v1:0 | 0.33 | 2.75 | 0.0825 |
| nova-pro | us.amazon.nova-pro-v1:0 | 0.80 | 3.20 | 0.20 |
| claude-haiku | us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0 | 1.10 | 5.50 | 0.11 |
| claude-sonnet-4.6 | us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6 | 3.30 | 16.50 | 0.33 |
| claude-opus-4.6 | us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-6-v1 | 5.50 | 27.50 | 0.55 |

The three Claude rates are exactly 10% above Anthropic's first-party list (Haiku 4.5 1/5, Sonnet 4.6 3/15, Opus 4.6 5/25, from Anthropic's model table). Use the gateway rates in tally.yaml for gateway tiers, since that is what is billed.

Schema: tiers now carry a required `provider` string (commit 3dae374, pushed). A tier is {name, harness, model, provider, price{input, cachedInput, output per MTok}, ceilingFraction}.

**Still unverified:**
- Whether AO's usage endpoint reports tokens and cost for a gateway worker. No gateway worker could be spawned. Expect tokens to appear (AO read them for subscription sessions) and cost to be null for unknown model ids; this is a guess.
- The AWS public price page did not render the Nova or current Claude rows when fetched, so the Nova list prices are confirmed only against the gateway.
- Sonnet 4.6 and Opus 4.6 through Claude Code (only claude-haiku was run; same path, higher cost).
- Nova on a real multi-file task. No prompt caching was seen for Nova, so long sessions resend the full context each turn.

**Decision needed:** may the gateway key be stored in an AO project's env (`ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`)? If yes, the working shape is one AO project per gateway tier (env: base URL, token, `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`, and `CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=8000` for Nova). If no, the alternative is a small local proxy run by Tally that holds the key and forwards to the gateway, with a dummy token in AO; that would also let Tally meter and cap spend per worker itself.

## fly-doom-jev test check

**Answer:** The suite passes in a fresh clone; every test file is fast and self-contained enough to be a pass/fail check.

**Evidence:**

- Fresh clone at f99b54c in ~/tally-scratch. Nothing was changed on GitHub.
- `make setup` -> 54 s (uv venv with Python 3.14.8, `uv pip install -e ".[dev]"`).
- `make test` -> `90 passed in 7.53s` (8.9 s wall) on the first run, `90 passed in 1.02s` on the second. 0 skipped. README says 89.
- Needs: uv, Python 3.14 (pyproject allows >=3.12), Apple clang. The C kernel builds itself on the first test run into engine/native/build (gitignored). No network, no API key (Jev is mocked), no data download: the 231 MB processed connectome is committed.
- Costs: clone took about 12 minutes (311 MB pack, 695 MB on disk). .venv is 453 MB and every worker worktree needs its own `make setup`. Working tree stays clean after tests.
- Per file, run alone (all under 0.5 s): test_bridge_guard 4, test_decoder 7, test_engine 3, test_full_connectome 6, test_graph 5, test_hf_export 1, test_jev 10, test_jev_live 14, test_plasticity 12, test_recording 2, test_reflexes 10, test_state_encoder 3, test_viz_export 3, test_weighting 9 (tests/unit), test_closed_loop 1 (tests/integration).

**Still unverified:** `make setup` inside an AO worker worktree (expected to work; not run). Behaviour on Linux or without clang.

# Sample tally.yaml for the finished-run fixture.
# The repository, test command and tiers below are examples; Tally reads all
# of them from this file and assumes nothing about the target repository.
version: 1

repo:
  path: .
  slug: acme/payments-service
  baseBranch: main

test:
  setupCommand: npm ci
  command: npm test
  timeoutSec: 900

backlog:
  source: github-issues
  issueLabel: tally

# Ordered from cheapest to strongest. Escalation moves one step right.
# provider is who serves and bills the model (anthropic, openai, litellm, ...).
# price is the published list price in USD per million tokens; check it
# against the provider's pricing page before a real run.
# ceilingFraction is the share of the size ceiling a tier may spend.
tiers:
  - name: cheap
    harness: claude-code
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
    price: { inputUsdPerMTok: 1.00, cachedInputUsdPerMTok: 0.10, outputUsdPerMTok: 5.00 }
    ceilingFraction: 0.2
  - name: middle
    harness: claude-code
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-sonnet-5-5
    price: { inputUsdPerMTok: 2.00, cachedInputUsdPerMTok: 0.20, outputUsdPerMTok: 10.00 }
    ceilingFraction: 0.5
  - name: top
    harness: claude-code
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-opus-5-5
    price: { inputUsdPerMTok: 4.00, cachedInputUsdPerMTok: 0.20, outputUsdPerMTok: 20.00 }
    ceilingFraction: 1.0

# What the strongest tier may spend on one task of each size, in USD.
ceilings:
  bySizeUsd: { small: 1.50, medium: 4.00, large: 10.00 }

budget:
  source: config
  usd: 40

concurrency: 3

integrations:
  neatlogs: true
  entire: true
  cfoai: false
  slack: false

# Sample tally.yaml for the finished-run fixture.
# The repository, test command and tiers below are examples; Tally reads all
# of them from this file and assumes nothing about the target repository.
version: 1

repo:
  path: .
  slug: acme/payments-service
  baseBranch: main

test:
  setupCommand: npm ci
  command: npm test
  timeoutSec: 900

backlog:
  source: github-issues
  issueLabel: tally

# Ordered from cheapest to strongest. Escalation moves one step right.
# provider is who serves and bills the model (anthropic, openai, litellm, ...).
# price is the published list price in USD per million tokens; check it
# against the provider's pricing page before a real run.
# ceilingFraction is the share of the size ceiling a tier may spend.
tiers:
  - name: cheap
    harness: claude-code
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
    price: { inputUsdPerMTok: 1.00, cachedInputUsdPerMTok: 0.10, outputUsdPerMTok: 5.00 }
    ceilingFraction: 0.2
  - name: middle
    harness: claude-code
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-sonnet-5-5
    price: { inputUsdPerMTok: 2.00, cachedInputUsdPerMTok: 0.20, outputUsdPerMTok: 10.00 }
    ceilingFraction: 0.5
  - name: top
    harness: claude-code
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-opus-5-5
    price: { inputUsdPerMTok: 4.00, cachedInputUsdPerMTok: 0.20, outputUsdPerMTok: 20.00 }
    ceilingFraction: 1.0

# What the strongest tier may spend on one task of each size, in USD.
ceilings:
  bySizeUsd: { small: 1.50, medium: 4.00, large: 10.00 }

budget:
  source: config
  usd: 40

concurrency: 3

integrations:
  neatlogs: true
  entire: true
  cfoai: false
  slack: false

item.stdout:
# Tally

A CFO for a fleet of coding agents. Give it a backlog and a budget. It sizes
each task, sends it to the cheapest model likely to finish it, stops any task
that overruns its spend ceiling, hands failed work to a stronger model, and
ends with a ledger tying every dollar to a merged PR.

Status: early scaffold. The shared data contract and the CLI entry point
exist; the commands are stubs.

## Setup

Needs Node 20 or later.

```bash
npm install
npm test          # unit tests
npm run build     # compile to dist/
node bin/tally.js --help
```

During development, `npm run tally -- <command>` runs the CLI from source.

## Commands

| Command | What it will do |
|---|---|
| `tally run` | Run the backlog against the budget in `tally.yaml`. Flags: `--dry-run`, `--budget <usd>`, `--only <task>`, `--baseline`, `--config <path>`. |
| `tally demo` | Run the full loop with simulated workers on a sample backlog. No accounts or keys. |
| `tally init` | Detect the test command, ask for a budget and issue label, and write `tally.yaml`. |
| `tally doctor` | One line per integration: connected, missing or broken, with the fix. |

## Layout

| Folder | Holds |
|---|---|
| `schema/` | The contract every part reads: TypeScript types, JSON Schema, validators, and a sample finished run in `schema/fixtures/finished-run/`. |
| `engine/` | The run loop, run state and ledger. |
| `adapters/` | One thin module per outside tool (Agent Orchestrator, Entire, neatlogs, cfo.ai, GitHub). |
| `agent/` | The CFO agent: sizing, routing, ceilings, escalation. |
| `cli/` | The `tally` command. |
| `dashboard/` | Static page that reads the ledger and run state. |
| `demo/` | Sample backlog and scripted outcomes for `tally demo`. |

## Configuration

Tally assumes nothing about the repository it works on. The repository, test
command, model tiers, list prices, ceilings and budget all come from
`tally.yaml` (a tier is a name, harness, model id, provider, list price and ceiling share); see `schema/fixtures/finished-run/tally.yaml` for a complete
example and `schema/tally-config.schema.json` for the rules.

Money in the ledger and run state is stored as integer nanos of USD
(1 USD = 1,000,000,000). Cost is always tokens multiplied by the list price in
`tally.yaml`.

## Secrets

Keys live in `~/.tally/.env`, outside every repository, and are loaded from
there. Never put them in this repo; `.env` files are git-ignored.

# Tally: implementation plan

Written 10 Oct 2026, 16:00 IST. Submission closes 12 Oct, 23:55 IST (about 56 hours).

Tally is a CFO for a fleet of coding agents. You give it a backlog and a budget. It sizes each task, gives it to the cheapest model likely to finish it, stops any task that overruns its ceiling, hands failed work to a stronger model, and ends with a ledger tying every dollar to a merged PR.

Nothing in this document is built yet. Command names are proposals.

## 1. What the judges score, and what earns it

| Criterion | Weight | What Tally must show |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | A full run on a real backlog: plan, route, execute, verify, recover, finish. Measured against a baseline. |
| Use of neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | Each product makes a decision possible at runtime, not just during the build. |
| Demo video | 20% | The dashboard tells the story: a routing decision, a stopped runaway, an escalation, the ledger. |
| Building in public | 15% | Posts tagged #neatHack through the build, using dashboard screenshots and real numbers. |

Written 10 Oct 2026, 16:00 IST. Submission closes 12 Oct, 23:55 IST (about 56 hours).

Tally is a CFO for a fleet of coding agents. You give it a backlog and a budget. It sizes each task, gives it to the cheapest model likely to finish it, stops any task that overruns its ceiling, hands failed work to a stronger model, and ends with a ledger tying every dollar to a merged PR.

Nothing in this document is built yet. Command names are proposals.

## 1. What the judges score, and what earns it

| Criterion | Weight | What Tally must show |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | A full run on a real backlog: plan, route, execute, verify, recover, finish. Measured against a baseline. |
| Use of neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | Each product makes a decision possible at runtime, not just during the build. |
| Demo video | 20% | The dashboard tells the story: a routing decision, a stopped runaway, an escalation, the ledger. |
| Building in public | 15% | Posts tagged #neatHack through the build, using dashboard screenshots and real numbers. |
| Usefulness and originality | 10% | "They cap people, we cap tasks", backed by the Uber, Meta and Gartner evidence. |

Evidence the submission needs: two sets of neatlogs traces with compared numbers, a run where an action failed and what happened next, Entire checkpoints or entire-graph output, a cfo.ai business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway), a public repo with commits dated in the hackathon, and #neatHack links.

## 2. Features

### V1: the loop works end to end (target: 11 Oct, 14:00 IST)

| # | Feature | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Backlog intake | Reads GitHub issues with a label; a YAML file is the fallback and the rerun format. |
| 2 | Task sizing | Runs entire-graph on each task to estimate files touched and dependents, and labels it small, medium or large. |
| 3 | CFO agent | An LLM agent that picks a model per task from the size, a price table and the budget left, and writes its reason in one sentence. |
| 4 | Fleet execution | Spawns one Agent Orchestrator worker per task with the chosen model, in its own branch. |
| 5 | Verification | A task passes only if the repo's tests pass for that task. The agent's own claim is not accepted. |
| 6 | Per-task spend ceiling | Each task gets a ceiling from its size. A watcher stops the worker when it is crossed. |
| 7 | Escalation | A failed or stopped task goes to the next model up, once, if budget allows. |
| 8 | Ledger | One row per attempt: task, size, model, tokens, cost, result, PR link. Saved as JSON. |
| 9 | Live dashboard | Budget bar, task rows with the decision sentence, and the ledger. Runs locally. |
| 10 | Tracing | Every CFO-agent decision and every worker run is traced in neatlogs from the first run. |
| 11 | Dry-run mode | Fake workers with scripted outcomes, costing nothing, so the loop and dashboard can be tested freely. |

### Final: everything furnished (target: 12 Oct, 12:00 IST)

| # | Feature | What it adds |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | Routing from history | The CFO agent uses real cost and pass rate per task size and model from earlier runs, replacing the static price table. |
| 13 | Handoff, not restart | Escalation passes the Entire handoff summary and the saved branch, so the stronger model continues the work. |
| 14 | Live budget in cfo.ai | Budget is read from a cfo.ai scenario; actual cost is written back after each task. |
| 15 | Baseline mode | `--baseline` sends every task to the top model, for the before/after comparison. |
| 16 | Experiment report | Runs each mode more than once and reports cost per merged PR, pass rate and spread. |
| 17 | Trace and checkpoint links | Every dashboard row links to its neatlogs trace, Entire checkpoint and PR. |
| 18 | Hosted dashboard | Public URL on AWS showing the recorded final runs. |
| 19 | Market list | CrustData search for engineering teams adopting coding agents, feeding market size into the plan. |
| 20 | Business plan | cfo.ai model with pricing, costs, revenue and runway. |
| 21 | Budget-low alert | One Slack webhook message when a run ends or budget drops below a threshold. Cut first if time is short. |

Tally drives coding agents on the user's own machine, so it is installed, not hosted. A judge gets three ways in, from no effort to full use:

| # | Way in | What it needs | What they see |
|---|---|---|---|
| 22 | Hosted dashboard | A browser | Our recorded runs: the ledger, the decisions, links to traces and checkpoints. Read-only. |
| 23 | `tally demo` | Node only. No accounts, no keys. | The full loop with simulated workers on a sample backlog, in the live dashboard. About two minutes. |
| 24 | `tally init` in their repo | Agent Orchestrator, plus whichever of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai they have | Tally running their agents on their issues. |

What makes way 24 work:

| # | Feature | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 25 | Setup wizard (`tally init`) | Detects the repo's test command, asks for a budget and an issue label, and connects each product in turn: neatlogs key, `entire enable`, the cfo.ai login. Writes `tally.yaml`. |
| 26 | Health check (`tally doctor`) | One line per product: connected, missing, or broken, with the exact command to fix it. |
| 27 | Config file (`tally.yaml`) | Test command, model tiers with their harness and list price, ceilings, budget source. Any harness Agent Orchestrator supports can be a tier. |
| 28 | Each product optional | Without cfo.ai the budget is a number in the config. Without neatlogs, history is local only. Without Entire, sizing falls back to code search and escalation restarts. The dashboard shows which are off. |
| 29 | Quickstart in the README | Install to first run in under ten commands, with the three ways in at the top. |

Logins, multi-user support, creating tasks in a browser, a Slack bot, a hosted service that runs agents on someone else's repo, and more than one escalation step.

```
GitHub issues ──▶ Intake ──▶ Sizer (entire-graph) ──▶ CFO agent ──▶ AO worker (chosen model)
                                                        ▲   ▲              │

                                                                     │            │
                                                                  passed        failed / over ceiling
                                                                     │            │

                                                    │                 Entire handoff ──▶ stronger model
                                                    ▼
                                                dashboard

- **Adapters**: one thin module per outside tool (Agent Orchestrator, Entire, neatlogs, cfo.ai, GitHub). The engine never calls a tool directly, so a tool that misbehaves can be swapped for its fallback.
- **CFO agent**: the only place an LLM makes a spending decision.
- **Watcher**: polls each running worker's token use and enforces the ceiling.
- **Dashboard**: a static page that reads the ledger and run state. It never writes.
- **Demo target**: `Vaibhaav-Tiwari/fly-doom-jev` (Python, 16 test files run with `make test`), with the backlog filed as issues on it. Collaborators' repos can be added later as further targets.

The CFO agent sends a task to the cheap model only when the expected cost is lower than going straight to the top model:

    cheap ceiling + P(cheap fails) x top cost  <  top cost

Three things keep this true in practice:

1. **The cheap attempt is capped.** Its ceiling is set as a fraction of what the top model would cost for that task (default 20%). So the most a wrong guess can add to any task is 20%, and that worst case is known before the run starts.
2. **Only confident tasks go cheap.** The sizer scores each task (files touched, dependents, whether tests already exist for the area, how specific the issue is). Tasks the CFO agent is unsure about go to the middle or top model directly.
3. **It learns.** Every result updates the failure rate for that task size and model. If cheap keeps failing on a class of task, the rule stops sending that class there.

Handoff lowers the cost further, because the stronger model starts from the failed attempt's branch and summary instead of from nothing.

## 4. Unknowns to settle first (spikes, 16:30–19:30 IST today)

Each has a fallback so nothing here can block V1.

| S6 | Can an agent write a value into a cfo.ai scenario through the MCP server after one browser login? | Tally writes a CSV that is imported into cfo.ai after each run. |

| Lane | Owns | Order of work |
|---|---|---|

| C: Dashboard and demo | `dashboard/`, `demo/` | Dashboard against dry-run data, the backlog of issues on the target repo, trace and checkpoint links, AWS hosting. |

| When | Milestone | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| 10 Oct 16:30–19:30 | Spikes done; schema agreed; Entire enabled on the repo; target repo chosen. | Findings note. |
| 10 Oct 19:30–11 Oct 02:00 | Engine, dashboard and CFO agent working in dry-run mode. | Dry run shows a routed, failed, escalated and passed task on the dashboard. |

| 11 Oct 22:00–12 Oct 08:00 | Experiment: baseline runs and Tally runs. | Comparison report from neatlogs traces. |
| 12 Oct 08:00–12:00 | **Final**: hosted dashboard, CrustData list, business plan. Feature freeze at 12:00. | Public URL. Plan in cfo.ai. |
| 12 Oct 12:00–19:00 | Record and edit the demo video; finish hackathon.md and evidence links. | Video file. |
| 12 Oct 19:00–22:00 | Submit. Three hours of slack before the 23:55 cutoff. | Submission confirmation. |

If the plan slips, cut in this order: Slack alert, AWS hosting (show the dashboard locally), third repeat of each run, live cfo.ai write (use the CSV fallback). Never cut the forced-failure run or the baseline comparison; both are named evidence.

## 7. The experiment

- **Backlog**: 7 tasks on the demo target: 3 small, 3 medium, 1 that looks medium but is hard.
- **Before**: every task on the top model, no ceilings.
- **After**: the same tasks routed by Tally.
- **Repeats**: 2 of each, 3 if time allows. One run each proves nothing, because token use on identical tasks can vary widely.
- **Reported**: cost per merged PR, pass rate, total cost, and the spread across repeats. Every run is published, including any where Tally loses.
- **Reset**: each run starts from the same commit of the demo target.

Tally never runs more than 3 workers at once. The experiment is 7 tasks x 2 modes x 2 repeats = 28 task runs in total, taken three at a time, one after another. At roughly 10 to 15 minutes a task that is about two to three hours. A third repeat adds 14 more runs and is done only if time allows.

## 8. How you test it

- **cfo.ai model skeleton**: budget, actuals, pricing, revenue and runway, so the agent has cells to write into.

Also yours: choosing the target repo for the backlog, posting the #neatHack updates, recording the video.

## 10. Risks

- **Routing may save less than hoped.** The routing rule in section 3 caps the loss from a wrong guess at 20% per task, so the downside is bounded. The size of the saving is still unknown until the experiment runs, and the result is published either way.
- **No Anthropic API key.** Workers and the CFO agent run on the Claude Code (Pro) and Codex subscriptions. Cost in the ledger is AO's estimated cost at list price, not money actually billed, and the video must say so. Pro-plan usage limits may pause workers mid-run, especially on the top model; Codex models are the relief.
- **The target repo's tests are unverified.** `fly-doom-jev` has a pytest suite, but it needs Python 3.14, a native kernel build and possibly large data files. Whether the tests run cleanly in a fresh worker checkout is the first thing to check. It has no open issues, so the backlog has to be written.
- **The failure scene may not happen naturally.** A prepared scenario (T4, a ceiling set too low on one task) produces it, and the video says that is what was done.
- **Sizing may misjudge tasks.** A task that looks small but is not will fail on the cheap model. The cap limits the cost, and the backlog includes one such task on purpose.

item.stdout:
# ao session

Manage agent sessions: list, inspect, rename, kill, restore, exit or resume an
agent, switch harnesses, clean up, and claim PRs.

## In-app session links

When referring a user or another agent to a session in AO Chat or the AO
terminal, emit this canonical link:

```text
ao://sessions/{project-id}/{session-id}
```

- Use stable IDs returned by `ao project ls` and `ao session ls`, or the current
  session's `AO_PROJECT_ID` and `AO_SESSION_ID`. Never use display names as
  identity; renaming a session must not change its link.
- Treat the project ID and session ID as separate URL path segments. Encode
  either ID with URL percent encoding if it contains characters that are not
  safe in one segment.
- Emit only the navigation route above. Do not append query strings, fragments,
  action names, credentials, authorities, or extra path segments.
- The link is handled only inside a currently running AO desktop app. It is not
  an operating-system protocol link and must not be described as supporting
  cold launch or navigation from external applications.
- A session link navigates; it never sends a message, executes a command, or
  performs another action.

Example for project `mercury` and session `mer-3`:

```text
ao://sessions/mercury/mer-3
```

## Syntax

```
ao session <subcommand> [args] [flags]
```

## Subcommands

---

### ao session ls

List sessions.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session ls [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `-a, --all` | Include orchestrator sessions | - |
| `--include-terminated` | Include terminated sessions | - |
| `--json` | Output as JSON | - |
| `-p, --project string` | Filter by project ID | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# List all active worker sessions
ao session ls
```

```bash
# List all sessions including terminated, scoped to one project
ao session ls --include-terminated -p agent-orchestrator
```

---

### ao session get

Fetch one session.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session get <id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Output as JSON | - |
| `-p, --project string` | Project id to scope the lookup | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Get details for session mer-3
ao session get mer-3
```

```bash
# Get session details as JSON
ao session get mer-3 --json
```

---

### ao session kill

Terminate a session.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session kill <id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `-p, --project string` | Project id to scope the lookup | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Kill session mer-3
ao session kill mer-3
```

---

### ao session rename

Rename a worker session. The project orchestrator cannot be renamed, including by itself; the daemon refuses with `ORCHESTRATOR_RENAME_UNSUPPORTED`.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session rename <id> <name> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `-p, --project string` | Project id to scope the lookup | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Rename session mer-3 to a new display name
ao session rename mer-3 "fix-auth-bug"
```

---

### ao session restore

Restore a terminated session or resume an exited agent.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session restore <id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `-p, --project string` | Project id to scope the lookup | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Restore a terminated session
ao session restore mer-3
```

---

### ao session exit-agent

Exit an agent without terminating its AO session. The session can later be
resumed in place.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session exit-agent <id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Output as JSON | - |
| `-p, --project string` | Project id to scope the lookup | - |

---

### ao session resume-agent

Resume an exited agent in its existing AO session.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session resume-agent <id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Output as JSON | - |
| `-p, --project string` | Project id to scope the lookup | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
ao session exit-agent mer-3
ao session resume-agent mer-3
```

---

### ao session switch-agent

Switch a running session to another installed agent harness. This preserves the
AO session while provisioning the target harness.

**Syntax:**
```
ao session switch-agent <id> <target-harness> [flags]

# Tally demo backlog.
# This file is intentionally self-contained: `tally demo` can replay the
# scripted outcomes below without GitHub, Agent Orchestrator, neatlogs, Entire,
# cfo.ai, or API keys.
version: 1
kind: tally-demo-backlog

repo:
  slug: demo/invoice-ledger
  baseBranch: main
  description: A tiny billing service used only by the simulated demo runner.

test:
  setupCommand: null
  command: npm test

tasks:
  - id: T1
    title: Round invoice totals to cents before writing ledger rows
    size: small
    issueNumber: 101
    description: |
      The invoice writer currently stores floating point totals directly in
      ledger rows. Update it so subtotal, tax, and total are rounded to two
      decimal places before persistence, without changing the tax rate.
    passCheck: npm test -- --run tests/invoice-rounding.test.ts
    outcomes: [passed]
    scriptedOutcome:
      route: cheap
      decision: Small arithmetic fix with a focused unit test, so the cheap tier should finish it inside the small ceiling.
      attempts:
        - tier: cheap
          result: passed
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 15200, cachedInput: 2400, output: 730 }

  - id: T2
    title: Show customer name in the receipt email subject
    size: small
    issueNumber: 102
    description: |
      Receipt emails say "Your receipt is ready" for every customer. Include the
      customer display name in the subject while preserving the existing body
      template and fallback for missing names.
    passCheck: npm test -- --run tests/receipt-email.test.ts
    outcomes: [passed]
    scriptedOutcome:
      route: cheap
      decision: Template-only change with existing coverage, so the cheapest model is the right first attempt.
      attempts:
        - tier: cheap
          result: passed
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 11800, cachedInput: 2100, output: 520 }

  - id: T3
    title: Reject duplicate webhook deliveries by event id
    size: small
    issueNumber: 103
    description: |
      Payment webhooks can be delivered more than once. Add an idempotency guard
      keyed by the provider event id so duplicate deliveries do not create
      duplicate ledger entries.
    passCheck: npm test -- --run tests/webhook-idempotency.test.ts
    outcomes: [passed]
    scriptedOutcome:
      route: cheap
      decision: The affected code path is narrow and the test names the exact idempotency case, so start cheap.
      attempts:
        - tier: cheap
          result: passed
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 18400, cachedInput: 3200, output: 900 }

  - id: T4
    title: Add CSV export for the monthly ledger
    size: medium
    issueNumber: 104
    description: |
      Add a monthly CSV export endpoint for ledger rows. The file must include
      invoice id, customer, status, subtotal, tax, total, and paid_at, sorted by
      paid_at ascending.
    passCheck: npm test -- --run tests/monthly-export.test.ts
    outcomes: [passed]
    scriptedOutcome:
      route: middle
      decision: This touches route handling, query filtering, and formatting, so the middle tier is cheaper than risking a stopped cheap attempt.
      attempts:
        - tier: middle
          result: passed
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 32200, cachedInput: 5100, output: 1640 }

  - id: T5
    title: Cache exchange rates without serving stale conversions
    size: medium
    issueNumber: 105
    description: |
      Exchange-rate lookups are slow. Add a cache with a ten minute TTL, but
      make sure a failed refresh keeps the last good rate only when it is still
      inside the TTL.
    passCheck: npm test -- --run tests/exchange-rate-cache.test.ts
    outcomes: [stopped, passed]
    scriptedOutcome:
      route: middle
      decision: It looks like a bounded cache change, so the middle tier gets a capped attempt before escalation.
      attempts:
        - tier: middle
          result: stopped
          resultReason: Ceiling crossed while chasing stale-cache edge cases.
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 51200, cachedInput: 9800, output: 2740 }
        - tier: top
          result: passed
          handoff: entire-handoff
          decision: The first attempt hit its ceiling; continue the same branch with the top tier and the Entire handoff.
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 43800, cachedInput: 12100, output: 2180 }

  - id: T6
    title: Reconcile partial refunds against the original invoice
    size: medium
    issueNumber: 106
    description: |
      Partial refunds should reduce recognized revenue and mark the invoice as
      partially_refunded without deleting the original payment row. Add the
      reconciliation logic and cover a partial refund followed by full refund.
    passCheck: npm test -- --run tests/refund-reconciliation.test.ts
    outcomes: [failed, passed]
    scriptedOutcome:
      route: middle
      decision: Refund reconciliation crosses state transitions and accounting totals, so begin at the middle tier.
      attempts:
        - tier: middle
          result: failed
          resultReason: The first attempt missed the full-refund follow-up state.
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 46700, cachedInput: 6900, output: 2320 }
        - tier: top
          result: passed
          handoff: entire-handoff
          decision: The failing middle attempt exposed a hidden state-machine edge; continue with the top tier and the failure context.
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 52600, cachedInput: 13400, output: 2860 }

  - id: T7
    title: Support tax rules for every country in one change
    size: large
    issueNumber: 107
    description: |
      Add correct tax calculation for every country, including regional rules,
      filing thresholds, exemptions, and future law changes, with no external
      tax provider and no product decision about supported countries.
    passCheck: npm test -- --run tests/global-tax-rules.test.ts
    outcomes: [failed]
    scriptedOutcome:
      route: top
      decision: The request is underspecified and broad, so the strongest tier is the only reasonable attempt; it may still fail.
      attempts:
        - tier: top
          result: failed
          resultReason: The task is not solvable without scope and tax-policy inputs.
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 68400, cachedInput: 14200, output: 3900 }

# Tally

A CFO for a fleet of coding agents. Give it a backlog and a budget. It sizes
each task, sends it to the cheapest model likely to finish it, stops any task
that overruns its spend ceiling, hands failed work to a stronger model, and
ends with a ledger tying every dollar to a merged PR.

Status: early build. The shared data contract exists, `tally demo` runs a
simulated backlog, and `tally run --dry-run` writes run state plus a ledger from
a file-backed backlog. Real AO workers and external adapters are next.

## Setup

Needs Node 20 or later.

```bash
npm install
npm test          # unit tests
npm run build     # compile to dist/
node bin/tally.js --help
```

During development, `npm run tally -- <command>` runs the CLI from source. After
`npm run build`, `node bin/tally.js <command>` runs the compiled package entry.

## Commands

| Command | What it will do |
|---|---|
| `tally run` | Run the backlog against the budget in `tally.yaml`. Today this requires `--dry-run`. Flags: `--dry-run`, `--budget <usd>`, `--only <task>`, `--baseline`, `--config <path>`. |
| `tally demo` | Run the full loop with simulated workers on a sample backlog. No accounts or keys. Writes `.tally/runs/<run-id>/run.json` and `ledger.json`. |
| `tally init` | Detect the test command, ask for a budget and issue label, and write `tally.yaml`. |
| `tally doctor` | One line per integration: connected, missing or broken, with the fix. |

## Layout

| Folder | Holds |
|---|---|
| `schema/` | The contract every part reads: TypeScript types, JSON Schema, validators, and a sample finished run in `schema/fixtures/finished-run/`. |
| `engine/` | The run loop, run state and ledger. |
| `adapters/` | One thin module per outside tool (Agent Orchestrator, Entire, neatlogs, cfo.ai, GitHub). |
| `agent/` | The CFO agent: sizing, routing, ceilings, escalation. |
| `cli/` | The `tally` command. |
| `dashboard/` | Static page that reads the ledger and run state. |
| `demo/` | Sample backlog and scripted outcomes for `tally demo`. |

## Configuration

Tally assumes nothing about the repository it works on. The repository, test
command, model tiers, list prices, ceilings and budget all come from
`tally.yaml` (a tier is a name, harness, model id, provider, list price and ceiling share); see `schema/fixtures/finished-run/tally.yaml` for a complete
example and `schema/tally-config.schema.json` for the rules.

Money in the ledger and run state is stored as integer nanos of USD
(1 USD = 1,000,000,000). Cost is always tokens multiplied by the list price in
`tally.yaml`.

For dry runs, set `backlog.source: file` and point `backlog.file` at YAML like:

```yaml
tasks:
  - id: T1
    title: Add validation for empty player name
    size: small
    outcomes: [passed]
  - id: T2
    title: Persist settings after restart
    size: medium
    outcomes: [stopped, passed]
```

`outcomes` is optional and defaults to one passed simulated attempt.

## Secrets

Keys live in `~/.tally/.env`, outside every repository, and are loaded from
there. Never put them in this repo; `.env` files are git-ignored.

# Tally

A CFO for a fleet of coding agents. Give it a backlog and a budget. It sizes
each task, sends it to the cheapest model likely to finish it, stops any task
that overruns its spend ceiling, hands failed work to a stronger model, and
ends with a ledger tying every dollar to a merged PR.

Status: early build. The shared data contract exists, `tally demo` runs a
simulated backlog, and `tally run --dry-run` writes run state plus a ledger from
a file-backed backlog. Real AO workers and external adapters are next.

## Setup

Needs Node 20 or later.

```bash
npm install
npm test          # unit tests
npm run build     # compile to dist/
node bin/tally.js --help
```

During development, `npm run tally -- <command>` runs the CLI from source. After
`npm run build`, `node bin/tally.js <command>` runs the compiled package entry.

## Commands

| Command | What it will do |
|---|---|
| `tally run` | Run the backlog against the budget in `tally.yaml`. Today this requires `--dry-run`. Flags: `--dry-run`, `--budget <usd>`, `--only <task>`, `--baseline`, `--config <path>`. |
| `tally demo` | Run the full loop with simulated workers on a sample backlog. No accounts or keys. Writes `.tally/runs/<run-id>/run.json` and `ledger.json`. |
| `tally init` | Detect the test command, ask for a budget and issue label, and write `tally.yaml`. |
| `tally doctor` | One line per integration: connected, missing or broken, with the fix. |

## Layout

| Folder | Holds |
|---|---|
| `schema/` | The contract every part reads: TypeScript types, JSON Schema, validators, and a sample finished run in `schema/fixtures/finished-run/`. |
| `engine/` | The run loop, run state and ledger. |
| `adapters/` | One thin module per outside tool (Agent Orchestrator, Entire, neatlogs, cfo.ai, GitHub). |
| `agent/` | The CFO agent: sizing, routing, ceilings, escalation. |
| `cli/` | The `tally` command. |
| `dashboard/` | Static page that reads the ledger and run state. |
| `demo/` | Sample backlog and scripted outcomes for `tally demo`. |

## Configuration

Tally assumes nothing about the repository it works on. The repository, test
command, model tiers, list prices, ceilings and budget all come from
`tally.yaml` (a tier is a name, harness, model id, provider, list price and ceiling share); see `schema/fixtures/finished-run/tally.yaml` for a complete
example and `schema/tally-config.schema.json` for the rules.

Money in the ledger and run state is stored as integer nanos of USD
(1 USD = 1,000,000,000). Cost is always tokens multiplied by the list price in
`tally.yaml`.

For dry runs, set `backlog.source: file` and point `backlog.file` at YAML like:

```yaml
tasks:
  - id: T1
    title: Add validation for empty player name
    size: small
    outcomes: [passed]
  - id: T2
    title: Persist settings after restart
    size: medium
    outcomes: [stopped, passed]
```

`outcomes` is optional and defaults to one passed simulated attempt.

## Secrets

Keys live in `~/.tally/.env`, outside every repository, and are loaded from
there. Never put them in this repo; `.env` files are git-ignored.

# Draft backlog for https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/fly-doom-jev.
# Do not file these as issues until the user approves them. The checks below
# are based on a scratch clone at f99b54c, where `make test` passed.
version: 1
kind: tally-draft-backlog

repo:
  slug: Vaibhaav-Tiwari/fly-doom-jev
  baseBranch: main
  observedCommit: f99b54c

test:
  setupCommand: make setup
  command: make test
  notes: Fresh clone test result from lane A was 90 passed in 7.53s.

tasks:
  - id: FDJ-1
    title: Add replay loader coverage for malformed recording files
    size: small
    label: tally
    body: |
      The replay loader already rejects a recording with no header, but it does
      not have focused coverage for malformed JSONL rows or frame metadata with
      a missing pattern. Add defensive tests and the smallest loader changes
      needed so a bad recording reports a clear exception instead of failing
      later in the API.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_recording.py -q

  - id: FDJ-2
    title: Include goal fields in encoded state tests
    size: small
    label: tally
    body: |
      `EnvironmentState` has a `goal` field for E1M1 strategy, but the unit
      tests only assert the older threat and serialization fields. Add coverage
      proving that a goal dict can be attached, serialized, and omitted for
      ordinary arena observations without breaking the existing schema version.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_state_encoder.py -q

  - id: FDJ-3
    title: Test POST /new rejects unknown live scenarios
    size: small
    label: tally
    body: |
      The live API validates scenario names in `request_new_episode`, but there
      is no direct API-level test for a bad `POST /new` body. Add a small test
      around the FastAPI route or the loop method so an unknown scenario returns
      a clear error and leaves the current scenario unchanged.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_jev_live.py -q

  - id: FDJ-4
    title: Preserve recording summary when both summary and episode_end rows exist
    size: medium
    label: tally
    body: |
      `load_recording` treats both `summary` and `episode_end` rows as the
      recording summary. Make the behavior explicit and deterministic when a
      file contains both rows, then add a regression test that documents which
      one wins and why. Keep the public replay response shape unchanged.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_recording.py tests/integration/test_closed_loop.py -q

  - id: FDJ-5
    title: Add action-weighting regression for missing MOVEMENT_INTENT metadata
    size: medium
    label: tally
    body: |
      `jev_action_weights` reads optional movement-intent probabilities from
      decision metadata. Add coverage for decisions that have probabilities but
      no `choice_probabilities` key, and make the implementation tolerate that
      shape without changing the existing weighting semantics.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_weighting.py tests/unit/test_jev.py -q

  - id: FDJ-6
    title: Make plasticity checkpoint errors actionable
    size: medium
    label: tally
    body: |
      A corrupt or incompatible plasticity checkpoint should fail with a message
      that names the checkpoint path and provenance mismatch instead of a raw
      NumPy exception. Add tests for corrupt checkpoint data and mismatched
      config hashes, then keep the fresh-start fallback for ordinary provenance
      mismatch.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plasticity.py -q

  - id: FDJ-7
    title: Add deterministic featured-recording generation for the static showcase
    size: medium
    difficultyNote: looks medium but is hard
    label: tally
    body: |
      The project now serves a static GitHub Pages showcase from curated
      recordings. Add a deterministic packaging path that writes `featured.json`
      in a stable order, verifies every referenced recording and frame exists,
      and fails loudly when a curated bundle is incomplete. This looks medium
      because it is packaging code, but it crosses replay metadata, static
      assets, and CLI behavior.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_recording.py tests/unit/test_hf_export.py -q

content.text: [from neatlogs-hack-8] From the orchestrator, correction to your current task; the human is unhappy with this and he is right. On main there are two separate pipelines. engine/real.ts is the proper loop (sizeTask, routeTask/routeBaseline, CeilingWatcher, decideEscalation, adapters behind ports). The dry-run branch of runTally in engine/run.ts is a second, hand-written simulation: it takes size from the backlog file, picks a tier with tierFor, invents cost with simulatedCost/simulatedTokens, writes its own decision sentence, and never calls the CFO agent. runDemo on top of it writes a hard-coded 3-task backlog and config to a temp dir. So the dry run and the demo do not exercise the loop that the real run uses, which is the whole point of plan feature 11. Fix it properly instead of only swapping the backlog: (1) Dry-run must be the SAME loop as the real run, runRealTally, with only the outside world faked: a scripted WorkerPort, usage port, session control and verifier whose outcomes, token use and timing come from the backlog's scripted outcomes, plus the offline sizing fallback and a file or in-memory history. Sizing, routing, ceilings, the watcher stopping an over-ceiling attempt, escalation, budget checks and the decision sentence all come from agent/ exactly as in a real run. Ledger rows from fakes stay marked costSource simulated. (2) Delete the separate simulation path and its helpers (tierFor, simulatedCost, simulatedTokens, the local decision function, the duplicate integrationStates) once nothing uses them. (3) tally demo is just that dry-run with demo/tally.yaml and demo/sample-backlog.yaml; no embedded config or backlog in engine code. (4) If the 7-task sample no longer yields the T2 picture because real routing chooses differently from the scripted tiers, tell me what needs changing in demo/ and I will route it to lane C; do not bend the router to fit the sample. (5) Tests: one test that runs the dry-run through the real loop and asserts a routed task, a stopped-at-ceiling attempt, an escalation and a budget skip. Keep the stable latest-run path and the T3 write-up from my last message. Report when the PR is open.

# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"
- Optionally suggest a `prefix_rule` - this will be shown to the user with an option to persist the rule approval for future sessions.

If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with "require_escalated". ALWAYS proceed to use the `justification` parameter - do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.

## When to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)
- You need to run a GUI app (e.g., open/xdg-open/osascript) to open browsers or files.
