  description: A tiny billing service used only by the simulated demo runner.

test:
  setupCommand: null
  command: npm test

tasks:
  - id: T1
    title: Round invoice totals to cents before writing ledger rows
    size: small
    issueNumber: 101
    description: |
      The invoice writer currently stores floating point totals directly in
      ledger rows. Update it so subtotal, tax, and total are rounded to two
      decimal places before persistence, without changing the tax rate.
    passCheck: npm test -- --run tests/invoice-rounding.test.ts
    outcomes: [passed]
    scriptedOutcome:
      route: cheap
      decision: Small arithmetic fix with a focused unit test, so the cheap tier should finish it inside the small ceiling.
      attempts:
        - tier: cheap
          result: passed
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 15200, cachedInput: 2400, output: 730 }

  - id: T2
    title: Show customer name in the receipt email subject
    size: small
    issueNumber: 102
    description: |
      Receipt emails say "Your receipt is ready" for every customer. Include the
      customer display name in the subject while preserving the existing body
      template and fallback for missing names.
    passCheck: npm test -- --run tests/receipt-email.test.ts
    outcomes: [passed]
    scriptedOutcome:
      route: cheap
      decision: Template-only change with existing coverage, so the cheapest model is the right first attempt.
      attempts:
        - tier: cheap
          result: passed
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 11800, cachedInput: 2100, output: 520 }

  - id: T3
    title: Reject duplicate webhook deliveries by event id
    size: small
    issueNumber: 103
    description: |
      Payment webhooks can be delivered more than once. Add an idempotency guard
      keyed by the provider event id so duplicate deliveries do not create
      duplicate ledger entries.
    passCheck: npm test -- --run tests/webhook-idempotency.test.ts
    outcomes: [passed]
    scriptedOutcome:
      route: cheap
      decision: The affected code path is narrow and the test names the exact idempotency case, so start cheap.
      attempts:
        - tier: cheap
          result: passed
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 18400, cachedInput: 3200, output: 900 }

  - id: T4
    title: Add CSV export for the monthly ledger
    size: medium
    issueNumber: 104
    description: |
      Add a monthly CSV export endpoint for ledger rows. The file must include
      invoice id, customer, status, subtotal, tax, total, and paid_at, sorted by
      paid_at ascending.
    passCheck: npm test -- --run tests/monthly-export.test.ts
    outcomes: [passed]
    scriptedOutcome:
      route: middle
      decision: This touches route handling, query filtering, and formatting, so the middle tier is cheaper than risking a stopped cheap attempt.
      attempts:
        - tier: middle
          result: passed
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 32200, cachedInput: 5100, output: 1640 }

    title: Cache exchange rates without serving stale conversions
    size: medium
    issueNumber: 105
    description: |
      Exchange-rate lookups are slow. Add a cache with a ten minute TTL, but
      make sure a failed refresh keeps the last good rate only when it is still
      inside the TTL.
    passCheck: npm test -- --run tests/exchange-rate-cache.test.ts
    outcomes: [stopped, passed]
    scriptedOutcome:
      route: middle
      decision: It looks like a bounded cache change, so the middle tier gets a capped attempt before escalation.
      attempts:
        - tier: middle
          result: stopped
          resultReason: Ceiling crossed while chasing stale-cache edge cases.
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 51200, cachedInput: 9800, output: 2740 }
        - tier: top
          result: passed
          handoff: entire-handoff
          decision: The first attempt hit its ceiling; continue the same branch with the top tier and the Entire handoff.
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 43800, cachedInput: 12100, output: 2180 }

  - id: T6
    title: Reconcile partial refunds against the original invoice
    size: medium
    issueNumber: 106
    description: |
      Partial refunds should reduce recognized revenue and mark the invoice as
      partially_refunded without deleting the original payment row. Add the
      reconciliation logic and cover a partial refund followed by full refund.
    passCheck: npm test -- --run tests/refund-reconciliation.test.ts
    outcomes: [failed, passed]
    scriptedOutcome:
      route: middle
      decision: Refund reconciliation crosses state transitions and accounting totals, so begin at the middle tier.
      attempts:

          result: failed
          resultReason: The first attempt missed the full-refund follow-up state.
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 46700, cachedInput: 6900, output: 2320 }
        - tier: top
          result: passed
          handoff: entire-handoff
          decision: The failing middle attempt exposed a hidden state-machine edge; continue with the top tier and the failure context.
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 52600, cachedInput: 13400, output: 2860 }

    title: Support tax rules for every country in one change
    size: large
    issueNumber: 107
    description: |
      Add correct tax calculation for every country, including regional rules,
      filing thresholds, exemptions, and future law changes, with no external
      tax provider and no product decision about supported countries.

    outcomes: [failed]

# Draft backlog for https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/fly-doom-jev.
# Do not file these as issues until the user approves them. The checks below
# are based on a scratch clone at f99b54c, where `make test` passed.
version: 1
kind: tally-draft-backlog

repo:
  slug: Vaibhaav-Tiwari/fly-doom-jev
  baseBranch: main
  observedCommit: f99b54c

test:
  setupCommand: make setup
  command: make test
  notes: Fresh clone test result from lane A was 90 passed in 7.53s.

tasks:
  - id: FDJ-1
    title: Add replay loader coverage for malformed recording files
    size: small
    label: tally
    body: |
      The replay loader already rejects a recording with no header, but it does
      not have focused coverage for malformed JSONL rows or frame metadata with
      a missing pattern. Add defensive tests and the smallest loader changes
      needed so a bad recording reports a clear exception instead of failing
      later in the API.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_recording.py -q

  - id: FDJ-2
    title: Include goal fields in encoded state tests
    size: small
    label: tally
    body: |
      `EnvironmentState` has a `goal` field for E1M1 strategy, but the unit
      tests only assert the older threat and serialization fields. Add coverage
      proving that a goal dict can be attached, serialized, and omitted for
      ordinary arena observations without breaking the existing schema version.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_state_encoder.py -q

  - id: FDJ-3
    title: Test POST /new rejects unknown live scenarios
    size: small
    label: tally
    body: |
      The live API validates scenario names in `request_new_episode`, but there
      is no direct API-level test for a bad `POST /new` body. Add a small test
      around the FastAPI route or the loop method so an unknown scenario returns
      a clear error and leaves the current scenario unchanged.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_jev_live.py -q

  - id: FDJ-4
    title: Preserve recording summary when both summary and episode_end rows exist
    size: medium
    label: tally
    body: |
      `load_recording` treats both `summary` and `episode_end` rows as the
      recording summary. Make the behavior explicit and deterministic when a
      file contains both rows, then add a regression test that documents which
      one wins and why. Keep the public replay response shape unchanged.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_recording.py tests/integration/test_closed_loop.py -q

  - id: FDJ-5
    title: Add action-weighting regression for missing MOVEMENT_INTENT metadata
    size: medium
    label: tally
    body: |
      `jev_action_weights` reads optional movement-intent probabilities from
      decision metadata. Add coverage for decisions that have probabilities but
      no `choice_probabilities` key, and make the implementation tolerate that
      shape without changing the existing weighting semantics.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_weighting.py tests/unit/test_jev.py -q

  - id: FDJ-6
    title: Make plasticity checkpoint errors actionable
    size: medium
    label: tally
    body: |
      A corrupt or incompatible plasticity checkpoint should fail with a message
      that names the checkpoint path and provenance mismatch instead of a raw
      NumPy exception. Add tests for corrupt checkpoint data and mismatched
      config hashes, then keep the fresh-start fallback for ordinary provenance
      mismatch.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plasticity.py -q

  - id: FDJ-7
    title: Add deterministic featured-recording generation for the static showcase
    size: medium
    difficultyNote: looks medium but is hard
    label: tally
    body: |
      The project now serves a static GitHub Pages showcase from curated
      recordings. Add a deterministic packaging path that writes `featured.json`
      in a stable order, verifies every referenced recording and frame exists,
      and fails loudly when a curated bundle is incomplete. This looks medium
      because it is packaging code, but it crosses replay metadata, static
      assets, and CLI behavior.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_recording.py tests/unit/test_hf_export.py -q

# Sample tally.yaml for the finished-run fixture.
# The repository, test command and tiers below are examples; Tally reads all
# of them from this file and assumes nothing about the target repository.
version: 1

repo:
  path: .
  slug: acme/payments-service
  baseBranch: main

test:
  setupCommand: npm ci
  command: npm test
  timeoutSec: 900

backlog:
  source: github-issues
  issueLabel: tally

# Ordered from cheapest to strongest. Escalation moves one step right.
# provider is who serves and bills the model (anthropic, openai, litellm, ...).
# price is the published list price in USD per million tokens; check it
# against the provider's pricing page before a real run.
# ceilingFraction is the share of the size ceiling a tier may spend.
tiers:
  - name: cheap
    harness: claude-code
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-haiku-4-5-20251001
    price: { inputUsdPerMTok: 1.00, cachedInputUsdPerMTok: 0.10, outputUsdPerMTok: 5.00 }
    ceilingFraction: 0.2
  - name: middle
    harness: claude-code
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-sonnet-5-5
    price: { inputUsdPerMTok: 2.00, cachedInputUsdPerMTok: 0.20, outputUsdPerMTok: 10.00 }
    ceilingFraction: 0.5
  - name: top
    harness: claude-code
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-opus-5-5
    price: { inputUsdPerMTok: 4.00, cachedInputUsdPerMTok: 0.20, outputUsdPerMTok: 20.00 }
    ceilingFraction: 1.0

# What the strongest tier may spend on one task of each size, in USD.
ceilings:
  bySizeUsd: { small: 1.50, medium: 4.00, large: 10.00 }

budget:
  source: config
  usd: 40

concurrency: 3

integrations:
  neatlogs: true
  entire: true
  cfoai: false
  slack: false

# Tally: implementation plan

Written 10 Oct 2026, 16:00 IST. Submission closes 12 Oct, 23:55 IST (about 56 hours).

Tally is a CFO for a fleet of coding agents. You give it a backlog and a budget. It sizes each task, gives it to the cheapest model likely to finish it, stops any task that overruns its ceiling, hands failed work to a stronger model, and ends with a ledger tying every dollar to a merged PR.

Nothing in this document is built yet. Command names are proposals.

## 1. What the judges score, and what earns it

| Criterion | Weight | What Tally must show |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | A full run on a real backlog: plan, route, execute, verify, recover, finish. Measured against a baseline. |
| Use of neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | Each product makes a decision possible at runtime, not just during the build. |
| Demo video | 20% | The dashboard tells the story: a routing decision, a stopped runaway, an escalation, the ledger. |
| Building in public | 15% | Posts tagged #neatHack through the build, using dashboard screenshots and real numbers. |
| Usefulness and originality | 10% | "They cap people, we cap tasks", backed by the Uber, Meta and Gartner evidence. |

Evidence the submission needs: two sets of neatlogs traces with compared numbers, a run where an action failed and what happened next, Entire checkpoints or entire-graph output, a cfo.ai business plan (pricing, costs, revenue, runway), a public repo with commits dated in the hackathon, and #neatHack links.

## 2. Features

### V1: the loop works end to end (target: 11 Oct, 14:00 IST)

| # | Feature | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Backlog intake | Reads GitHub issues with a label; a YAML file is the fallback and the rerun format. |
| 2 | Task sizing | Runs entire-graph on each task to estimate files touched and dependents, and labels it small, medium or large. |
| 3 | CFO agent | An LLM agent that picks a model per task from the size, a price table and the budget left, and writes its reason in one sentence. |
| 4 | Fleet execution | Spawns one Agent Orchestrator worker per task with the chosen model, in its own branch. |
| 5 | Verification | A task passes only if the repo's tests pass for that task. The agent's own claim is not accepted. |
| 6 | Per-task spend ceiling | Each task gets a ceiling from its size. A watcher stops the worker when it is crossed. |
| 7 | Escalation | A failed or stopped task goes to the next model up, once, if budget allows. |
| 8 | Ledger | One row per attempt: task, size, model, tokens, cost, result, PR link. Saved as JSON. |
| 9 | Live dashboard | Budget bar, task rows with the decision sentence, and the ledger. Runs locally. |
| 10 | Tracing | Every CFO-agent decision and every worker run is traced in neatlogs from the first run. |
| 11 | Dry-run mode | Fake workers with scripted outcomes, costing nothing, so the loop and dashboard can be tested freely. |

### Final: everything furnished (target: 12 Oct, 12:00 IST)

| # | Feature | What it adds |
|---|---|---|
| 12 | Routing from history | The CFO agent uses real cost and pass rate per task size and model from earlier runs, replacing the static price table. |
| 13 | Handoff, not restart | Escalation passes the Entire handoff summary and the saved branch, so the stronger model continues the work. |
| 14 | Live budget in cfo.ai | Budget is read from a cfo.ai scenario; actual cost is written back after each task. |
| 15 | Baseline mode | `--baseline` sends every task to the top model, for the before/after comparison. |
| 16 | Experiment report | Runs each mode more than once and reports cost per merged PR, pass rate and spread. |
| 17 | Trace and checkpoint links | Every dashboard row links to its neatlogs trace, Entire checkpoint and PR. |
| 18 | Hosted dashboard | Public URL on AWS showing the recorded final runs. |
| 19 | Market list | CrustData search for engineering teams adopting coding agents, feeding market size into the plan. |
| 20 | Business plan | cfo.ai model with pricing, costs, revenue and runway. |
| 21 | Budget-low alert | One Slack webhook message when a run ends or budget drops below a threshold. Cut first if time is short. |

### Usable by a judge on their own repo (part of Final)

Tally drives coding agents on the user's own machine, so it is installed, not hosted. A judge gets three ways in, from no effort to full use:

| # | Way in | What it needs | What they see |
|---|---|---|---|
| 22 | Hosted dashboard | A browser | Our recorded runs: the ledger, the decisions, links to traces and checkpoints. Read-only. |
| 23 | `tally demo` | Node only. No accounts, no keys. | The full loop with simulated workers on a sample backlog, in the live dashboard. About two minutes. |
| 24 | `tally init` in their repo | Agent Orchestrator, plus whichever of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai they have | Tally running their agents on their issues. |

What makes way 24 work:

| # | Feature | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| 25 | Setup wizard (`tally init`) | Detects the repo's test command, asks for a budget and an issue label, and connects each product in turn: neatlogs key, `entire enable`, the cfo.ai login. Writes `tally.yaml`. |
| 26 | Health check (`tally doctor`) | One line per product: connected, missing, or broken, with the exact command to fix it. |
| 27 | Config file (`tally.yaml`) | Test command, model tiers with their harness and list price, ceilings, budget source. Any harness Agent Orchestrator supports can be a tier. |
| 28 | Each product optional | Without cfo.ai the budget is a number in the config. Without neatlogs, history is local only. Without Entire, sizing falls back to code search and escalation restarts. The dashboard shows which are off. |
| 29 | Quickstart in the README | Install to first run in under ten commands, with the three ways in at the top. |

This costs roughly half a day of lane A and lane C time. The engine must therefore never hard-code the demo repo: repo, test command and tiers come from config from the first commit.

### Deliberately out
Logins, multi-user support, creating tasks in a browser, a Slack bot, a hosted service that runs agents on someone else's repo, and more than one escalation step.

## 3. How it fits together

```
GitHub issues ──▶ Intake ──▶ Sizer (entire-graph) ──▶ CFO agent ──▶ AO worker (chosen model)
                                                        ▲   ▲              │
                              price history (neatlogs) ─┘   │              ▼
                              budget left (cfo.ai) ─────────┘         Verifier (tests)
                                                                     │            │
                                                                  passed        failed / over ceiling
                                                                     │            │
                                        cost ──▶ ledger ──▶ cfo.ai   ◀┘            ▼
                                                    │                 Entire handoff ──▶ stronger model
                                                    ▼
                                                dashboard
```

Parts, each with one job:

- **Engine**: the run loop and state. Owns the ledger file.
- **Adapters**: one thin module per outside tool (Agent Orchestrator, Entire, neatlogs, cfo.ai, GitHub). The engine never calls a tool directly, so a tool that misbehaves can be swapped for its fallback.
- **CFO agent**: the only place an LLM makes a spending decision.
- **Watcher**: polls each running worker's token use and enforces the ceiling.
- **Dashboard**: a static page that reads the ledger and run state. It never writes.
- **Demo target**: `Vaibhaav-Tiwari/fly-doom-jev` (Python, 16 test files run with `make test`), with the backlog filed as issues on it. Collaborators' repos can be added later as further targets.

Stack: TypeScript on Node for the engine, adapters and CLI; a static HTML and JS dashboard with no framework; JSON files for state.

Model tiers come from `tally.yaml`. The main set is the seven models on the LiteLLM gateway, cheapest first: nova-micro, nova-lite, nova-2-lite, nova-pro, claude-haiku, claude-sonnet-4.6, claude-opus-4.6. These are paid per token, so the ledger can show real spend. Whether each can drive a coding worker under Agent Orchestrator is spike S7; any that cannot are still usable for the CFO agent's own sizing and routing calls. The Claude Code subscription models (Haiku 4.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, set through `ao spawn --model`) are the fallback set. Codex models are also available through `ao spawn --harness codex`; they slot into the same tiers once their list prices are confirmed, and a Claude Code to Codex escalation is the cross-agent handoff Entire documents.

### The routing rule, and why a failed cheap attempt cannot sink the run

The CFO agent sends a task to the cheap model only when the expected cost is lower than going straight to the top model:

    cheap ceiling + P(cheap fails) x top cost  <  top cost

Three things keep this true in practice:

1. **The cheap attempt is capped.** Its ceiling is set as a fraction of what the top model would cost for that task (default 20%). So the most a wrong guess can add to any task is 20%, and that worst case is known before the run starts.
2. **Only confident tasks go cheap.** The sizer scores each task (files touched, dependents, whether tests already exist for the area, how specific the issue is). Tasks the CFO agent is unsure about go to the middle or top model directly.
3. **It learns.** Every result updates the failure rate for that task size and model. If cheap keeps failing on a class of task, the rule stops sending that class there.

Handoff lowers the cost further, because the stronger model starts from the failed attempt's branch and summary instead of from nothing.

With a 20% cap, the cheap route breaks even when it fails about 80% of the time. Whether real failure rates sit below that on this backlog is what the experiment measures.

Cost is always tokens used multiplied by published list price. That keeps numbers comparable whether a worker runs on an API key or a subscription.

## 4. Unknowns to settle first (spikes, 16:30–19:30 IST today)

Each has a fallback so nothing here can block V1.

| # | Question | Fallback if the answer is no |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Can a script spawn an AO worker with a chosen model, read its status and result, and kill it? | `--model` exists on `ao spawn`. If status is hard to read, poll the worker's branch and PR instead. |
| S2 | Can token use for a running worker be read while it runs? | **Settled, yes.** The AO daemon serves `GET /api/v1/usage/sessions/{sessionId}` on localhost, returning live token totals and an estimated cost per session and per model for Claude Code and Codex. Checked against the running daemon on 10 Oct. The watcher polls this. |
| S3 | Does neatlogs expose past run cost and outcome through an API? | Tally keeps its own history file built from the same data; neatlogs remains the trace record and the evidence. |
| S4 | Does entire-graph give usable impact numbers from the CLI on a fresh repo? | Size tasks by counting files matched by a code search on the issue text. |
| S5 | Does the Entire handoff summary work when the next agent uses a different model? | Pass the failed session's summary from `entire checkpoint explain` plus the branch. |
| S6 | Can an agent write a value into a cfo.ai scenario through the MCP server after one browser login? | Tally writes a CSV that is imported into cfo.ai after each run. |

## 5. Work split

At most three AO workers run at any time, in three lanes. Each lane owns its own folders, so lanes do not edit the same files. The ledger and event schema is the first thing merged, because every other part reads it.

| Lane | Owns | Order of work |
|---|---|---|
| A: Engine | `engine/`, `cli/`, `adapters/` | Spikes S1–S6, then schema, run loop, ledger, dry-run mode, then the adapters (AO, Entire, GitHub, neatlogs, cfo.ai), then baseline mode and the experiment runner. |
| B: CFO agent | `agent/` | Sizer, routing rule, ceilings and the watcher, escalation and handoff, neatlogs tracing, history-based routing. |
| C: Dashboard and demo | `dashboard/`, `demo/` | Dashboard against dry-run data, the backlog of issues on the target repo, trace and checkpoint links, AWS hosting. |

Each piece of work is also a GitHub issue on the Tally repo, so human contributors can pick up an issue instead of an AO worker. A lane has one owner at a time, human or agent.

Each worker's PR gets AO's native review before merge.

## 6. Timeline (IST)

| When | Milestone | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| 10 Oct 16:30–19:30 | Spikes done; schema agreed; Entire enabled on the repo; target repo chosen. | Findings note. |
| 10 Oct 19:30–11 Oct 02:00 | Engine, dashboard and CFO agent working in dry-run mode. | Dry run shows a routed, failed, escalated and passed task on the dashboard. |
| 11 Oct 02:00–14:00 | **V1**: real workers on the demo backlog, traced in neatlogs. | One full real run with a ledger. First neatlogs traces. |
| 11 Oct 14:00–22:00 | History routing, Entire handoff, cfo.ai read and write, links. | A forced-failure run showing handoff. cfo.ai scenario updated by the agent. |
| 11 Oct 22:00–12 Oct 08:00 | Experiment: baseline runs and Tally runs. | Comparison report from neatlogs traces. |
| 12 Oct 08:00–12:00 | **Final**: hosted dashboard, CrustData list, business plan. Feature freeze at 12:00. | Public URL. Plan in cfo.ai. |
| 12 Oct 12:00–19:00 | Record and edit the demo video; finish hackathon.md and evidence links. | Video file. |
| 12 Oct 19:00–22:00 | Submit. Three hours of slack before the 23:55 cutoff. | Submission confirmation. |

If the plan slips, cut in this order: Slack alert, AWS hosting (show the dashboard locally), third repeat of each run, live cfo.ai write (use the CSV fallback). Never cut the forced-failure run or the baseline comparison; both are named evidence.

## 7. The experiment

- **Backlog**: 7 tasks on the demo target: 3 small, 3 medium, 1 that looks medium but is hard.
- **Before**: every task on the top model, no ceilings.
- **After**: the same tasks routed by Tally.
- **Repeats**: 2 of each, 3 if time allows. One run each proves nothing, because token use on identical tasks can vary widely.
- **Reported**: cost per merged PR, pass rate, total cost, and the spread across repeats. Every run is published, including any where Tally loses.
- **Reset**: each run starts from the same commit of the demo target.

Tally never runs more than 3 workers at once. The experiment is 7 tasks x 2 modes x 2 repeats = 28 task runs in total, taken three at a time, one after another. At roughly 10 to 15 minutes a task that is about two to three hours. A third repeat adds 14 more runs and is done only if time allows.

## 8. How you test it

Tests are ordered from cheapest to most expensive. Do not move to the next level until the current one passes.

| # | Test | How | Pass when |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Unit tests | `npm test` | Routing picks the expected model for each size and budget; ceiling maths and ledger totals are right. |
| T2 | Dry run | `tally run --dry-run --budget 40` | Dashboard shows all 7 tasks routed, one failing and escalating, the budget bar ending at the ledger total. Costs nothing. |
| T3 | One real task | `tally run --only <issue> --budget 5` | A worker opens a PR, tests pass, one ledger row appears, a trace appears in neatlogs, a checkpoint appears in Entire. |
| T4 | Forced failure | Run one medium task with a ceiling set far too low. | The worker is stopped at the ceiling, the ledger shows a stopped attempt, a stronger model picks up the same branch and finishes. This is the recovery evidence. |
| T5 | Budget too small | `tally run --budget 2` | Tally completes what it can, marks the rest "not started: no budget", and total cost stays under the budget. |
| T6 | Bad task | Include one issue that cannot be solved. | It fails on both models, is marked failed, and the run still finishes the other tasks. |
| T7 | Interrupted run | Kill Tally mid-run, then start it again. | It resumes from the ledger without redoing finished tasks or double-counting cost. |
| T8 | Full run | `tally run --budget 40` on all 7. | Every task is passed, failed or skipped with a reason; ledger total equals the sum of rows and matches cfo.ai. |
| T9 | Comparison | `tally experiment --repeats 2` | The report shows both modes with spread, and every number can be traced to a neatlogs trace. |
| T10 | Stranger install | A teammate who has not seen the code follows only the README on their own machine and repo. | `tally demo` works with no accounts; `tally doctor` names every missing piece correctly; `tally init` then `tally run` completes one task on a second repo. |
| T11 | Missing products | Run with each of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai switched off in turn. | The run still completes, and the dashboard says which product is off. |

### Evidence check, one per product
- **neatlogs**: open a trace for a CFO decision and one for a failed worker; the failure point is visible.
- **Entire**: `entire checkpoint list` shows checkpoints for worker sessions; the handoff summary for the T4 task exists.
- **cfo.ai**: the budget scenario shows a value the agent wrote; the business plan page exists and is shareable.
- **CrustData**: the search that produced the market list can be rerun and returns the same kind of results.
- **Repo**: commits are dated 10–12 Oct and the repo is public (it is now).

## 9. What only you can do

Already in place (checked 10 Oct): GitHub CLI logged in, Entire CLI logged in, the Tally repo is public.

Keys go in one file, `~/.tally/.env`, outside every repo so it cannot be committed and every worker can read it:

| Name | For | Needed by |
|---|---|---|
| `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` | Sending traces, reading run history | First real run |
| `CRUSTDATA_API_KEY` | Market list | Final |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_REGION=us-east-1` | Hosting the dashboard | Final. The AWS CLI also needs installing. |
| `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` | Optional alert | Only if the alert is built |

Two things need a browser and cannot be done by an agent:

- **cfo.ai**: run `claude mcp add --scope user --transport http cfoai https://api.cfo.ai/mcp`, then approve in the browser while logged in to cfo.ai. Until this is done Tally uses the CSV fallback, so nothing is blocked.
- **cfo.ai model skeleton**: budget, actuals, pricing, revenue and runway, so the agent has cells to write into.

Also yours: choosing the target repo for the backlog, posting the #neatHack updates, recording the video.

## 10. Risks

- **Routing may save less than hoped.** The routing rule in section 3 caps the loss from a wrong guess at 20% per task, so the downside is bounded. The size of the saving is still unknown until the experiment runs, and the result is published either way.
- **No Anthropic API key.** Workers and the CFO agent run on the Claude Code (Pro) and Codex subscriptions. Cost in the ledger is AO's estimated cost at list price, not money actually billed, and the video must say so. Pro-plan usage limits may pause workers mid-run, especially on the top model; Codex models are the relief.
- **The target repo's tests are unverified.** `fly-doom-jev` has a pytest suite, but it needs Python 3.14, a native kernel build and possibly large data files. Whether the tests run cleanly in a fresh worker checkout is the first thing to check. It has no open issues, so the backlog has to be written.
- **The failure scene may not happen naturally.** A prepared scenario (T4, a ceiling set too low on one task) produces it, and the video says that is what was done.
- **Sizing may misjudge tasks.** A task that looks small but is not will fail on the cheap model. The cap limits the cost, and the backlog includes one such task on purpose.

1. **The cheap attempt is capped.** Its ceiling is set as a fraction of what the top model would cost for that task (default 20%). So the most a wrong guess can add to any task is 20%, and that worst case is known before the run starts.
2. **Only confident tasks go cheap.** The sizer scores each task (files touched, dependents, whether tests already exist for the area, how specific the issue is). Tasks the CFO agent is unsure about go to the middle or top model directly.
3. **It learns.** Every result updates the failure rate for that task size and model. If cheap keeps failing on a class of task, the rule stops sending that class there.

Handoff lowers the cost further, because the stronger model starts from the failed attempt's branch and summary instead of from nothing.

With a 20% cap, the cheap route breaks even when it fails about 80% of the time. Whether real failure rates sit below that on this backlog is what the experiment measures.

Cost is always tokens used multiplied by published list price. That keeps numbers comparable whether a worker runs on an API key or a subscription.

Each has a fallback so nothing here can block V1.

| # | Question | Fallback if the answer is no |
|---|---|---|

Checked against the running daemon on 10 Oct. The watcher polls this. |
| S3 | Does neatlogs expose past run cost and outcome through an API? | Tally keeps its own history file built from the same data; neatlogs remains the trace record and the evidence. |
| S4 | Does entire-graph give usable impact numbers from the CLI on a fresh repo? | Size tasks by counting files matched by a code search on the issue text. |
| S5 | Does the Entire handoff summary work when the next agent uses a different model? | Pass the failed session's summary from `entire checkpoint explain` plus the branch. |
| S6 | Can an agent write a value into a cfo.ai scenario through the MCP server after one browser login? | Tally writes a CSV that is imported into cfo.ai after each run. |

At most three AO workers run at any time, in three lanes. Each lane owns its own folders, so lanes do not edit the same files. The ledger and event schema is the first thing merged, because every other part reads it.

| Lane | Owns | Order of work |
|---|---|---|
| A: Engine | `engine/`, `cli/`, `adapters/` | Spikes S1–S6, then schema, run loop, ledger, dry-run mode, then the adapters (AO, Entire, GitHub, neatlogs, cfo.ai), then baseline mode and the experiment runner. |
| B: CFO agent | `agent/` | Sizer, routing rule, ceilings and the watcher, escalation and handoff, neatlogs tracing, history-based routing. |
| C: Dashboard and demo | `dashboard/`, `demo/` | Dashboard against dry-run data, the backlog of issues on the target repo, trace and checkpoint links, AWS hosting. |

| When | Milestone | Proof |
|---|---|---|
| 10 Oct 16:30–19:30 | Spikes done; schema agreed; Entire enabled on the repo; target repo chosen. | Findings note. |
| 10 Oct 19:30–11 Oct 02:00 | Engine, dashboard and CFO agent working in dry-run mode. | Dry run shows a routed, failed, escalated and passed task on the dashboard. |

| 12 Oct 12:00–19:00 | Record and edit the demo video; finish hackathon.md and evidence links. | Video file. |
| 12 Oct 19:00–22:00 | Submit. Three hours of slack before the 23:55 cutoff. | Submission confirmation. |

- **Backlog**: 7 tasks on the demo target: 3 small, 3 medium, 1 that looks medium but is hard.
- **Before**: every task on the top model, no ceilings.
- **After**: the same tasks routed by Tally.
- **Repeats**: 2 of each, 3 if time allows. One run each proves nothing, because token use on identical tasks can vary widely.
- **Reported**: cost per merged PR, pass rate, total cost, and the spread across repeats. Every run is published, including any where Tally loses.
- **Reset**: each run starts from the same commit of the demo target.

Tests are ordered from cheapest to most expensive. Do not move to the next level until the current one passes.

| # | Test | How | Pass when |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 | Unit tests | `npm test` | Routing picks the expected model for each size and budget; ceiling maths and ledger totals are right. |
| T2 | Dry run | `tally run --dry-run --budget 40` | Dashboard shows all 7 tasks routed, one failing and escalating, the budget bar ending at the ledger total. Costs nothing. |
| T3 | One real task | `tally run --only <issue> --budget 5` | A worker opens a PR, tests pass, one ledger row appears, a trace appears in neatlogs, a checkpoint appears in Entire. |
| T4 | Forced failure | Run one medium task with a ceiling set far too low. | The worker is stopped at the ceiling, the ledger shows a stopped attempt, a stronger model picks up the same branch and finishes. This is the recovery evidence. |
| T5 | Budget too small | `tally run --budget 2` | Tally completes what it can, marks the rest "not started: no budget", and total cost stays under the budget. |
| T6 | Bad task | Include one issue that cannot be solved. | It fails on both models, is marked failed, and the run still finishes the other tasks. |
| T7 | Interrupted run | Kill Tally mid-run, then start it again. | It resumes from the ledger without redoing finished tasks or double-counting cost. |
| T8 | Full run | `tally run --budget 40` on all 7. | Every task is passed, failed or skipped with a reason; ledger total equals the sum of rows and matches cfo.ai. |
| T9 | Comparison | `tally experiment --repeats 2` | The report shows both modes with spread, and every number can be traced to a neatlogs trace. |
| T10 | Stranger install | A teammate who has not seen the code follows only the README on their own machine and repo. | `tally demo` works with no accounts; `tally doctor` names every missing piece correctly; `tally init` then `tally run` completes one task on a second repo. |
| T11 | Missing products | Run with each of neatlogs, Entire and cfo.ai switched off in turn. | The run still completes, and the dashboard says which product is off. |

- **neatlogs**: open a trace for a CFO decision and one for a failed worker; the failure point is visible.
- **Entire**: `entire checkpoint list` shows checkpoints for worker sessions; the handoff summary for the T4 task exists.
- **cfo.ai**: the budget scenario shows a value the agent wrote; the business plan page exists and is shareable.
- **CrustData**: the search that produced the market list can be rerun and returns the same kind of results.
- **Repo**: commits are dated 10–12 Oct and the repo is public (it is now).

## 9. What only you can do

Already in place (checked 10 Oct): GitHub CLI logged in, Entire CLI logged in, the Tally repo is public.

Keys go in one file, `~/.tally/.env`, outside every repo so it cannot be committed and every worker can read it:

| Name | For | Needed by |
|---|---|---|
| `NEATLOGS_API_KEY` | Sending traces, reading run history | First real run |
| `CRUSTDATA_API_KEY` | Market list | Final |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `AWS_REGION=us-east-1` | Hosting the dashboard | Final. The AWS CLI also needs installing. |
| `SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL` | Optional alert | Only if the alert is built |

Two things need a browser and cannot be done by an agent:

- **cfo.ai**: run `claude mcp add --scope user --transport http cfoai https://api.cfo.ai/mcp`, then approve in the browser while logged in to cfo.ai. Until this is done Tally uses the CSV fallback, so nothing is blocked.
- **cfo.ai model skeleton**: budget, actuals, pricing, revenue and runway, so the agent has cells to write into.

Also yours: choosing the target repo for the backlog, posting the #neatHack updates, recording the video.

## 10. Risks

- **Routing may save less than hoped.** The routing rule in section 3 caps the loss from a wrong guess at 20% per task, so the downside is bounded. The size of the saving is still unknown until the experiment runs, and the result is published either way.
- **No Anthropic API key.** Workers and the CFO agent run on the Claude Code (Pro) and Codex subscriptions. Cost in the ledger is AO's estimated cost at list price, not money actually billed, and the video must say so. Pro-plan usage limits may pause workers mid-run, especially on the top model; Codex models are the relief.
- **The target repo's tests are unverified.** `fly-doom-jev` has a pytest suite, but it needs Python 3.14, a native kernel build and possibly large data files. Whether the tests run cleanly in a fresh worker checkout is the first thing to check. It has no open issues, so the backlog has to be written.
- **The failure scene may not happen naturally.** A prepared scenario (T4, a ceiling set too low on one task) produces it, and the video says that is what was done.
- **Sizing may misjudge tasks.** A task that looks small but is not will fail on the cheap model. The cap limits the cost, and the backlog includes one such task on purpose.

Tally is a CFO for a fleet of coding agents. You give it a backlog and a budget. It sizes each task, gives it to the cheapest model likely to finish it, stops any task that overruns its ceiling, hands failed work to a stronger model, and ends with a ledger tying every dollar to a merged PR.

| Criterion | Weight | What Tally must show |
|---|---|---|
| The agent | 30% | A full run on a real backlog: plan, route, execute, verify, recover, finish. Measured against a baseline. |
| Use of neatlogs, Entire, cfo.ai | 25% | Each product makes a decision possible at runtime, not just during the build. |
| Demo video | 20% | The dashboard tells the story: a routing decision, a stopped runaway, an escalation, the ledger. |

The CFO agent sends a task to the cheap model only when the expected cost is lower than going straight to the top model:

    cheap ceiling + P(cheap fails) x top cost  <  top cost

1. **The cheap attempt is capped.** Its ceiling is set as a fraction of what the top model would cost for that task (default 20%). So the most a wrong guess can add to any task is 20%, and that worst case is known before the run starts.

Handoff lowers the cost further, because the stronger model starts from the failed attempt's branch and summary instead of from nothing.

With a 20% cap, the cheap route breaks even when it fails about 80% of the time. Whether real failure rates sit below that on this backlog is what the experiment measures.

description: "Catalog of the AO (Agent Orchestrator) `ao` CLI: spawning workers, managing sessions and projects, creating reusable Cues, sending messages, controlling the shared browser, previewing pages, and daemon control. Use when using the ao CLI, creating Cues, spawning workers, or managing AO sessions in an AO workspace."
trigger: "Using the ao CLI in an AO workspace: creating Cues, spawning workers, managing sessions/projects, sending messages, controlling or previewing pages."
---

# AO CLI Catalog

`ao` is a thin CLI over the local AO daemon. Every command is `ao <command> --help` for the authoritative flag list.

| Command | What it does | When to use | Details |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spawn` | Spawn a project worker, orchestrator, or projectless standalone worker | Starting a new task or issue | [commands/spawn.md](commands/spawn.md) |
| `session` | Manage agent sessions (list, kill, rename, restore, etc.) | Inspecting or controlling running/terminated sessions | [commands/session.md](commands/session.md) |
| `agent` | Inspect installed harnesses and launch readiness | Choosing or diagnosing an agent harness | `ao agent ls --refresh` |
| `pr` | Merge a PR or resolve its review threads | Completing a reviewed change | `ao pr merge` / `ao pr resolve-comments` |
| `project` | Register, inspect, configure, or remove projects | Setting up or managing repos AO knows about | [commands/project.md](commands/project.md) |
| `automation` | Manage durable recurring session automations | Creating, editing, disabling, deleting, and inspecting scheduled runs | [commands/automation.md](commands/automation.md) |
| `cue` | Create or list reusable project Cues | Saving a repetitive command or agent task at the user's request | [commands/cue.md](commands/cue.md) |
| `orchestrator` | List orchestrator sessions | Viewing which sessions are orchestrators | [commands/orchestrator.md](commands/orchestrator.md) |
| `review` | Start, list, cancel, or submit AO's native reviewer for a worker's PR (default: this session) | Getting an adversarial review of an AO session's PR; never spawn a worker to review | [commands/review.md](commands/review.md) |
| `send` | Send a message to a running agent session | Correcting or directing a live agent | [commands/send.md](commands/send.md) |
| `report` | Persist a meaningful worker report | Checkpoints, blockers, decisions, outputs, and completion | [commands/report.md](commands/report.md) |
| `preview` | Start a session-owned app or open an exact URL/file | Running and showing the worker's relevant app, Markdown, HTML, PDF, or image | [commands/preview.md](commands/preview.md) |
| `render` | Show a self-contained HTML page inline in a chat thread | Answering with a chart, table, diagram, or mockup | [commands/render.md](commands/render.md) |
| `browser` | Inspect and control the session's shared live browser | Verifying a web app through snapshots, interactions, waits, screenshots, console, and errors | [commands/browser.md](commands/browser.md) |
| `start` | Fetch (if needed) and open the AO desktop app | Launching the app | [commands/start.md](commands/start.md) |
| `stop` | Stop the AO daemon | Shutting down AO | [commands/stop.md](commands/stop.md) |
| `status` | Show daemon status | Verifying the daemon is up and healthy | [commands/status.md](commands/status.md) |
| `doctor` | Run local health checks | Diagnosing AO setup problems | [commands/doctor.md](commands/doctor.md) |
| `import` | Import projects from a legacy AO install | Migrating from the old flat-file store | [commands/import.md](commands/import.md) |
| `version` | Print version information | Checking installed version | - |
| `completion` | Generate shell completion scripts | Setting up tab completion | - |

## Conventions

- Most read commands accept `--json` for machine-readable output.
- `-p / --project` scopes session subcommand lookups to one project.
- Session and project ids are shown by `ao session ls` and `ao project ls`.
- To refer to a session in AO Chat or the AO terminal, use the canonical in-app
  link `ao://sessions/{project-id}/{session-id}`. Read
  [commands/session.md](commands/session.md) for identity, encoding, and safety
  rules before constructing one.
- When the user asks to save a repeatable task as a Cue, use `ao cue list --json` to check existing definitions, then `ao cue create`. An agent Cue stores a reusable instruction; a command Cue stores an exact shell command. This agent-facing command can create and read Cues, but cannot edit or delete them. Direct the user to project settings for changes to existing Cues.
- `--agent` is an alias for `--harness` on `ao spawn`.
- Every command accepts `-h / --help` for the full flag list.
- For frontend launch, preview selection, or artifact handoff, read
  [commands/preview.md](commands/preview.md) before acting. Its static-file,
  project-runtime, and automatic-handoff rules are load-bearing.
- For page inspection, interaction, or request diagnosis, read
  [commands/browser.md](commands/browser.md). It defines shared-tab behavior
  and the opt-in network policy.

Use [references.md](references.md) only when a natural-language request does
not map clearly to a command above.

# ao project

Manage projects: register repos, inspect, configure per-project settings, and remove.

## Syntax

```
ao project <subcommand> [args] [flags]
```

## Subcommands

---

### ao project add

Register a local git repo as a project so sessions can be spawned in it. The path must be an existing git repository on disk. With `--as-workspace`, the path may be a parent folder containing direct child git repositories; AO initializes/adopts the parent as the root repo and gitignores children.

**Syntax:**
```
ao project add [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--as-workspace` | Register a parent folder as a workspace project (root-as-repo plus direct child repos) | - |
| `--id string` | Project id | Derived by the daemon from the path |
| `--name string` | Display name | - |
| `--orchestrator-agent string` | Default orchestrator session agent | - |
| `--path string` | Absolute path to the local git repo | Required |
| `--worker-agent string` | Default worker session agent | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Register a repo as a project
ao project add --path /path/to/agent-orchestrator --name "agent-orchestrator"
```

```bash
# Register a workspace (parent folder containing multiple repos)
ao project add --path /path/to/side-quests --as-workspace --name "side-quests"
```

---

### ao project ls

List registered projects. Aliases: `ls`, `list`.

**Syntax:**
```
ao project ls [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Output projects as JSON | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# List all registered projects
ao project ls
```

---

### ao project get

Fetch one registered project.

**Syntax:**
```
ao project get <id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Output project as JSON | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Get details for the agent-orchestrator project
ao project get agent-orchestrator
```

---

### ao project rm

Remove a registered project. Aliases: `rm`, `remove`, `delete`.

**Syntax:**
```
ao project rm <id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Output removal result as JSON | - |
| `-y, --yes` | Skip confirmation prompt | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Remove a project (with confirmation)
ao project rm agent-orchestrator
```

```bash
# Remove without prompt
ao project rm agent-orchestrator -y
```

---

### ao project set-config

Replace a project's saved configuration. AO reads these settings when it spawns a session. Use flags for common fields or `--config-json` for the full object. `--clear` removes all configuration.

**Warning:** This command replaces the whole config, even when you use focused flags. The CLI silently ignores unknown keys in `--config-json`, so a typo can leave the replacement empty. Its config mirror also omits `effort`; `ao project get --json` cannot show it, and a CLI configuration replacement drops existing effort values. Use Project Settings in the desktop app or the daemon API when you need to preserve or change effort. See the [full-config warning](https://docs.orchestrator.inc/configuration/projects/#update-from-the-cli) before updating project settings from the CLI.

**Syntax:**
```
ao project set-config <id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--agent-rules string` | Project-specific standing instructions appended to worker session prompts | - |
| `--agent-rules-file string` | Repo-relative file containing project-specific worker standing instructions | - |
| `--canonical-repo-url string` | Explicit upstream HTTPS repository URL used for PR claims (same provider, host, and port as `origin`) | - |
| `--clear` | Clear all config | - |
| `--config-json string` | Full config as a JSON object (overrides field flags) | - |
| `--default-branch string` | Base branch new session worktrees are created from | - |
| `--env stringArray` | Env var `KEY=VALUE` forwarded into sessions (repeatable) | - |
| `--json` | Output the updated project as JSON | - |
| `--model string` | Agent model override (e.g. `claude-opus-4-5`) | - |
| `--orchestrator-agent string` | Harness override for orchestrator sessions | - |
| `--orchestrator-rules string` | Project-specific standing instructions appended to orchestrator session prompts | - |
| `--permission string` | Permission mode: `default`, `accept-edits`, `auto`, `bypass-permissions` | - |
| `--post-create stringArray` | Command to run after workspace creation (repeatable) | - |
| `--session-prefix string` | Displayed session-id prefix | - |
| `--symlink stringArray` | Repo-relative path to symlink into workspaces (repeatable) | - |
| `--tracker-assignee string` | Issue assignee required for tracker intake eligibility | - |
| `--tracker-intake` | Opt this project into GitHub or GitLab issue intake; inert unless the daemon also has `AO_TRACKER_INTAKE=on` | Disabled |
| `--tracker-repo string` | Provider-native issue repository (`owner/repo` or `group/subgroup/repo`); defaults to the Git origin | - |
| `--reviewer stringArray` | Reviewer harness for worker PRs (repeatable) | - |
| `--worker-agent string` | Harness override for worker sessions | - |

Use `--config-json` for fields without a dedicated flag, including
`trackerIntake.provider`, `autoReview`, `containerReap.disabled`,
`agentConfig.mode`, `worker.agentConfig.mode`, and
`orchestrator.agentConfig.mode`. The full-config replacement warning above
still applies.

**Examples:**

```bash
# Set default branch and model for a project
ao project set-config agent-orchestrator --default-branch main --model claude-opus-4-5
```

```bash
# Replace the complete config; include every setting you want to keep
ao project set-config agent-orchestrator --config-json \
  '{"defaultBranch":"main","agentConfig":{"model":"claude-opus-4-5"}}'
```

```bash
# Set an env var and a post-create command
ao project set-config agent-orchestrator --env "NODE_ENV=development" --post-create "npm install"
```

```bash
# Set worker and orchestrator standing rules
ao project set-config agent-orchestrator --agent-rules "Run focused tests before reporting done." --orchestrator-rules "Delegate implementation work to worker sessions."
```

```bash
# Load worker rules from a repo-relative file
ao project set-config agent-orchestrator --agent-rules-file docs/ao-worker-rules.md
```

```bash
# Enable assignee-scoped issue intake (requires AO_TRACKER_INTAKE=on)
ao project set-config agent-orchestrator --tracker-intake \
  --tracker-repo owner/repo --tracker-assignee alice
```

# ao project

Manage projects: register repos, inspect, configure per-project settings, and remove.

## Syntax

```
ao project <subcommand> [args] [flags]
```

## Subcommands

---

### ao project add

Register a local git repo as a project so sessions can be spawned in it. The path must be an existing git repository on disk. With `--as-workspace`, the path may be a parent folder containing direct child git repositories; AO initializes/adopts the parent as the root repo and gitignores children.

**Syntax:**
```
ao project add [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--as-workspace` | Register a parent folder as a workspace project (root-as-repo plus direct child repos) | - |
| `--id string` | Project id | Derived by the daemon from the path |
| `--name string` | Display name | - |
| `--orchestrator-agent string` | Default orchestrator session agent | - |
| `--path string` | Absolute path to the local git repo | Required |
| `--worker-agent string` | Default worker session agent | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Register a repo as a project
ao project add --path /path/to/agent-orchestrator --name "agent-orchestrator"
```

```bash
# Register a workspace (parent folder containing multiple repos)
ao project add --path /path/to/side-quests --as-workspace --name "side-quests"
```

---

### ao project ls

List registered projects. Aliases: `ls`, `list`.

**Syntax:**
```
ao project ls [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Output projects as JSON | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# List all registered projects
ao project ls
```

---

### ao project get

Fetch one registered project.

**Syntax:**
```
ao project get <id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Output project as JSON | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Get details for the agent-orchestrator project
ao project get agent-orchestrator
```

---

### ao project rm

Remove a registered project. Aliases: `rm`, `remove`, `delete`.

**Syntax:**
```
ao project rm <id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--json` | Output removal result as JSON | - |
| `-y, --yes` | Skip confirmation prompt | - |

**Examples:**

```bash
# Remove a project (with confirmation)
ao project rm agent-orchestrator
```

```bash
# Remove without prompt
ao project rm agent-orchestrator -y
```

---

### ao project set-config

Replace a project's saved configuration. AO reads these settings when it spawns a session. Use flags for common fields or `--config-json` for the full object. `--clear` removes all configuration.

**Warning:** This command replaces the whole config, even when you use focused flags. The CLI silently ignores unknown keys in `--config-json`, so a typo can leave the replacement empty. Its config mirror also omits `effort`; `ao project get --json` cannot show it, and a CLI configuration replacement drops existing effort values. Use Project Settings in the desktop app or the daemon API when you need to preserve or change effort. See the [full-config warning](https://docs.orchestrator.inc/configuration/projects/#update-from-the-cli) before updating project settings from the CLI.

**Syntax:**
```
ao project set-config <id> [flags]
```

**Flags:**

| Flag | Meaning | Default / Required |
|---|---|---|
| `--agent-rules string` | Project-specific standing instructions appended to worker session prompts | - |
| `--agent-rules-file string` | Repo-relative file containing project-specific worker standing instructions | - |
| `--canonical-repo-url string` | Explicit upstream HTTPS repository URL used for PR claims (same provider, host, and port as `origin`) | - |
| `--clear` | Clear all config | - |
| `--config-json string` | Full config as a JSON object (overrides field flags) | - |
| `--default-branch string` | Base branch new session worktrees are created from | - |
| `--env stringArray` | Env var `KEY=VALUE` forwarded into sessions (repeatable) | - |
| `--json` | Output the updated project as JSON | - |
| `--model string` | Agent model override (e.g. `claude-opus-4-5`) | - |
| `--orchestrator-agent string` | Harness override for orchestrator sessions | - |
| `--orchestrator-rules string` | Project-specific standing instructions appended to orchestrator session prompts | - |
| `--permission string` | Permission mode: `default`, `accept-edits`, `auto`, `bypass-permissions` | - |
| `--post-create stringArray` | Command to run after workspace creation (repeatable) | - |
| `--session-prefix string` | Displayed session-id prefix | - |
| `--symlink stringArray` | Repo-relative path to symlink into workspaces (repeatable) | - |
| `--tracker-assignee string` | Issue assignee required for tracker intake eligibility | - |
| `--tracker-intake` | Opt this project into GitHub or GitLab issue intake; inert unless the daemon also has `AO_TRACKER_INTAKE=on` | Disabled |
| `--tracker-repo string` | Provider-native issue repository (`owner/repo` or `group/subgroup/repo`); defaults to the Git origin | - |
| `--reviewer stringArray` | Reviewer harness for worker PRs (repeatable) | - |
| `--worker-agent string` | Harness override for worker sessions | - |

Use `--config-json` for fields without a dedicated flag, including
`trackerIntake.provider`, `autoReview`, `containerReap.disabled`,
`agentConfig.mode`, `worker.agentConfig.mode`, and
`orchestrator.agentConfig.mode`. The full-config replacement warning above
still applies.

# Set default branch and model for a project
ao project set-config agent-orchestrator --default-branch main --model claude-opus-4-5

```bash

ao project set-config agent-orchestrator --config-json \

```bash

ao project set-config agent-orchestrator --agent-rules "Run focused tests before reporting done." --orchestrator-rules "Delegate implementation work to worker sessions."

```bash
# Load worker rules from a repo-relative file
ao project set-config agent-orchestrator --agent-rules-file docs/ao-worker-rules.md

```bash

ao project set-config agent-orchestrator --tracker-intake \

# Escalation Requests

Commands are run outside the sandbox if they are approved by the user, or match an existing rule that allows it to run unrestricted. The command string is split into independent command segments at shell control operators, including but not limited to:

- Pipes: |
- Logical operators: &&, ||
- Command separators: ;
- Subshell boundaries: (...), $(...)

Each resulting segment is evaluated independently for sandbox restrictions and approval requirements.

Example:

git pull | tee output.txt

This is treated as two command segments:

["git", "pull"]

["tee", "output.txt"]

Commands that use more advanced shell features like redirection (>, >>, <), substitutions ($(...), ...), environment variables (FOO=bar), or wildcard patterns (*, ?) will not be evaluated against rules, to limit the scope of what an approved rule allows.

## How to request escalation

IMPORTANT: To request approval to execute a command that will require escalated privileges:

- Provide the `sandbox_permissions` parameter with the value `"require_escalated"`
- Include a short question asking the user if they want to allow the action in `justification` parameter. e.g. "Do you want to download and install dependencies for this project?"
- Optionally suggest a `prefix_rule` - this will be shown to the user with an option to persist the rule approval for future sessions.

If you run a command that is important to solving the user's query, but it fails because of sandboxing or with a likely sandbox-related network error (for example DNS/host resolution, registry/index access, or dependency download failure), rerun the command with "require_escalated". ALWAYS proceed to use the `justification` parameter - do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.

## When to request escalation

While commands are running inside the sandbox, here are some scenarios that will require escalation outside the sandbox:

- You need to run a command that writes to a directory that requires it (e.g. running tests that write to /var)
- You need to run a GUI app (e.g., open/xdg-open/osascript) to open browsers or files.

ALWAYS proceed to use the `sandbox_permissions` and `justification` parameters. do not message the user before requesting approval for the command.
- You are about to take a potentially destructive action such as an `rm` or `git reset` that the user did not explicitly ask for.
- Be judicious with escalating, but if completing the user's request requires it, you should do so - don't try and circumvent approvals by using other tools.

## prefix_rule guidance

When choosing a `prefix_rule`, request one that will allow you to fulfill similar requests from the user in the future without re-requesting escalation. It should be categorical and reasonably scoped to similar capabilities. You should rarely pass the entire command into `prefix_rule`.

NEVER provide a prefix_rule if your command uses a heredoc or herestring.

ceilings:
  bySizeUsd: { small: 1.50, medium: 4.00, large: 10.00 }

budget:
  source: config
  usd: 40

concurrency: 3

integrations:
  neatlogs: true
  entire: true
  cfoai: false
  slack: false

# Draft backlog for https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/fly-doom-jev.
# Do not file these as issues until the user approves them. The checks below
# are based on a scratch clone at f99b54c, where `make test` passed.
version: 1
kind: tally-draft-backlog

repo:
  slug: Vaibhaav-Tiwari/fly-doom-jev
  baseBranch: main
  observedCommit: f99b54c

test:
  setupCommand: make setup
  command: make test
  notes: Fresh clone test result from lane A was 90 passed in 7.53s.

tasks:
  - id: FDJ-1
    title: Add replay loader coverage for malformed recording files
    size: small
    label: tally
    body: |
      The replay loader already rejects a recording with no header, but it does
      not have focused coverage for malformed JSONL rows or frame metadata with
      a missing pattern. Add defensive tests and the smallest loader changes
      needed so a bad recording reports a clear exception instead of failing
      later in the API.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_recording.py -q

  - id: FDJ-2
    title: Include goal fields in encoded state tests
    size: small
    label: tally
    body: |
      `EnvironmentState` has a `goal` field for E1M1 strategy, but the unit
      tests only assert the older threat and serialization fields. Add coverage
      proving that a goal dict can be attached, serialized, and omitted for
      ordinary arena observations without breaking the existing schema version.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_state_encoder.py -q

  - id: FDJ-3
    title: Test POST /new rejects unknown live scenarios
    size: small
    label: tally
    body: |
      The live API validates scenario names in `request_new_episode`, but there
      is no direct API-level test for a bad `POST /new` body. Add a small test
      around the FastAPI route or the loop method so an unknown scenario returns
      a clear error and leaves the current scenario unchanged.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_jev_live.py -q

  - id: FDJ-4
    title: Preserve recording summary when both summary and episode_end rows exist
    size: medium
    label: tally
    body: |
      `load_recording` treats both `summary` and `episode_end` rows as the
      recording summary. Make the behavior explicit and deterministic when a
      file contains both rows, then add a regression test that documents which
      one wins and why. Keep the public replay response shape unchanged.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_recording.py tests/integration/test_closed_loop.py -q

  - id: FDJ-5
    title: Add action-weighting regression for missing MOVEMENT_INTENT metadata
    size: medium
    label: tally
    body: |
      `jev_action_weights` reads optional movement-intent probabilities from
      decision metadata. Add coverage for decisions that have probabilities but
      no `choice_probabilities` key, and make the implementation tolerate that
      shape without changing the existing weighting semantics.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_weighting.py tests/unit/test_jev.py -q

  - id: FDJ-6
    title: Make plasticity checkpoint errors actionable
    size: medium
    label: tally
    body: |
      A corrupt or incompatible plasticity checkpoint should fail with a message
      that names the checkpoint path and provenance mismatch instead of a raw
      NumPy exception. Add tests for corrupt checkpoint data and mismatched
      config hashes, then keep the fresh-start fallback for ordinary provenance
      mismatch.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_plasticity.py -q

  - id: FDJ-7
    title: Add deterministic featured-recording generation for the static showcase
    size: medium
    difficultyNote: looks medium but is hard
    label: tally
    body: |
      The project now serves a static GitHub Pages showcase from curated
      recordings. Add a deterministic packaging path that writes `featured.json`
      in a stable order, verifies every referenced recording and frame exists,
      and fails loudly when a curated bundle is incomplete. This looks medium
      because it is packaging code, but it crosses replay metadata, static
      assets, and CLI behavior.
    passCheck: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit/test_recording.py tests/unit/test_hf_export.py -q

# Ordered from cheapest to strongest. Escalation moves one step right.
# provider is who serves and bills the model (anthropic, openai, litellm, ...).

  - name: middle
    harness: claude-code
    provider: anthropic
    model: claude-sonnet-5-5
    price: { inputUsdPerMTok: 2.00, cachedInputUsdPerMTok: 0.20, outputUsdPerMTok: 10.00 }
    ceilingFraction: 0.5

ceilings:

budget:
  source: config
  usd: 40

concurrency: 3

  neatlogs: true

  slack: false

item.stdout:
# Tally

A CFO for a fleet of coding agents. Give it a backlog and a budget. It sizes
each task, sends it to the cheapest model likely to finish it, stops any task
that overruns its spend ceiling, hands failed work to a stronger model, and
ends with a ledger tying every dollar to a merged PR.

Status: early build. The shared data contract exists, `tally demo` runs the
seven-task simulated demo backlog, and `tally run --dry-run` writes run state
plus a ledger from a file-backed backlog. The real AO worker path is wired and
ready for a gated one-task smoke run.

## Setup

Needs Node 20 or later.

```bash
npm install
npm test          # unit tests
npm run build     # compile to dist/
node bin/tally.js --help
```

During development, `npm run tally -- <command>` runs the CLI from source. After
`npm run build`, `node bin/tally.js <command>` runs the compiled package entry.

## Commands

| Command | What it will do |
|---|---|
| `tally run` | Run the backlog against the budget in `tally.yaml`. Flags: `--dry-run`, `--budget <usd>`, `--only <task>`, `--baseline`, `--config <path>`. |
| `tally demo` | Run the full loop with simulated workers on `demo/tally.yaml` and `demo/sample-backlog.yaml`. No accounts or keys. Writes `.tally/runs/<run-id>/run.json` and `ledger.json`. |
| `tally init` | Detect the test command, ask for a budget and issue label, and write `tally.yaml`. |
| `tally doctor` | One line per integration: connected, missing or broken, with the fix. |

## Layout

| Folder | Holds |
|---|---|
| `schema/` | The contract every part reads: TypeScript types, JSON Schema, validators, and a sample finished run in `schema/fixtures/finished-run/`. |
| `engine/` | The run loop, run state and ledger. |
| `adapters/` | One thin module per outside tool (Agent Orchestrator, Entire, neatlogs, cfo.ai, GitHub). |
| `agent/` | The CFO agent: sizing, routing, ceilings, escalation. |
| `cli/` | The `tally` command. |
| `dashboard/` | Static page that reads the ledger and run state. |
| `demo/` | Sample backlog and scripted outcomes for `tally demo`. |

## Configuration

Tally assumes nothing about the repository it works on. The repository, test
command, model tiers, list prices, ceilings and budget all come from
`tally.yaml` (a tier is a name, harness, model id, provider, list price and ceiling share); see `schema/fixtures/finished-run/tally.yaml` for a complete
example and `schema/tally-config.schema.json` for the rules.

Money in the ledger and run state is stored as integer nanos of USD
(1 USD = 1,000,000,000). Cost is always tokens multiplied by the list price in
`tally.yaml`.

For dry runs, set `backlog.source: file` and point `backlog.file` at YAML like:

```yaml
tasks:
  - id: T1
    title: Add validation for empty player name
    size: small
    outcomes: [passed]
  - id: T2
    title: Persist settings after restart
    size: medium
    outcomes: [stopped, passed]
```

`outcomes` is optional and defaults to one passed simulated attempt.

The latest run is also mirrored to `.tally/runs/latest/run.json` and
`.tally/runs/latest/ledger.json` so the dashboard has one stable path to poll.

## Secrets

Keys live in `~/.tally/.env`, outside every repository, and are loaded from
there. Never put them in this repo; `.env` files are git-ignored.

# Tally

A CFO for a fleet of coding agents. Give it a backlog and a budget. It sizes
each task, sends it to the cheapest model likely to finish it, stops any task
that overruns its spend ceiling, hands failed work to a stronger model, and
ends with a ledger tying every dollar to a merged PR.

Status: early build. The shared data contract exists, `tally demo` runs the
seven-task simulated demo backlog, and `tally run --dry-run` writes run state
plus a ledger from a file-backed backlog. The real AO worker path is wired and
ready for a gated one-task smoke run.

## Setup

Needs Node 20 or later.

```bash
npm install
npm test          # unit tests
npm run build     # compile to dist/
node bin/tally.js --help
```

During development, `npm run tally -- <command>` runs the CLI from source. After
`npm run build`, `node bin/tally.js <command>` runs the compiled package entry.

## Commands

| Command | What it will do |
|---|---|
| `tally run` | Run the backlog against the budget in `tally.yaml`. Flags: `--dry-run`, `--budget <usd>`, `--only <task>`, `--baseline`, `--config <path>`. |
| `tally demo` | Run the full loop with simulated workers on `demo/tally.yaml` and `demo/sample-backlog.yaml`. No accounts or keys. Writes `.tally/runs/<run-id>/run.json` and `ledger.json`. |
| `tally init` | Detect the test command, ask for a budget and issue label, and write `tally.yaml`. |
| `tally doctor` | One line per integration: connected, missing or broken, with the fix. |

## Layout

| Folder | Holds |
|---|---|
| `schema/` | The contract every part reads: TypeScript types, JSON Schema, validators, and a sample finished run in `schema/fixtures/finished-run/`. |
| `engine/` | The run loop, run state and ledger. |
| `adapters/` | One thin module per outside tool (Agent Orchestrator, Entire, neatlogs, cfo.ai, GitHub). |
| `agent/` | The CFO agent: sizing, routing, ceilings, escalation. |
| `cli/` | The `tally` command. |
| `dashboard/` | Static page that reads the ledger and run state. |
| `demo/` | Sample backlog and scripted outcomes for `tally demo`. |

## Configuration

Tally assumes nothing about the repository it works on. The repository, test
command, model tiers, list prices, ceilings and budget all come from
`tally.yaml` (a tier is a name, harness, model id, provider, list price and ceiling share); see `schema/fixtures/finished-run/tally.yaml` for a complete
example and `schema/tally-config.schema.json` for the rules.

Money in the ledger and run state is stored as integer nanos of USD
(1 USD = 1,000,000,000). Cost is always tokens multiplied by the list price in
`tally.yaml`.

For dry runs, set `backlog.source: file` and point `backlog.file` at YAML like:

```yaml
tasks:
  - id: T1
    title: Add validation for empty player name
    size: small
    outcomes: [passed]
  - id: T2
    title: Persist settings after restart
    size: medium
    outcomes: [stopped, passed]
```

`outcomes` is optional and defaults to one passed simulated attempt.

The latest run is also mirrored to `.tally/runs/latest/run.json` and
`.tally/runs/latest/ledger.json` so the dashboard has one stable path to poll.

## Secrets

Keys live in `~/.tally/.env`, outside every repository, and are loaded from
there. Never put them in this repo; `.env` files are git-ignored.

# Tally demo backlog.
# This file is intentionally self-contained: `tally demo` can replay the
# scripted outcomes below without GitHub, Agent Orchestrator, neatlogs, Entire,
# cfo.ai, or API keys.
version: 1
kind: tally-demo-backlog

repo:
  slug: demo/invoice-ledger
  baseBranch: main
  description: A tiny billing service used only by the simulated demo runner.

test:
  setupCommand: null
  command: npm test

tasks:
  - id: T1
    title: Round invoice totals to cents before writing ledger rows
    size: small
    issueNumber: 101
    description: |
      The invoice writer currently stores floating point totals directly in
      ledger rows. Update it so subtotal, tax, and total are rounded to two
      decimal places before persistence, without changing the tax rate.
    passCheck: npm test -- --run tests/invoice-rounding.test.ts
    outcomes: [passed]
    scriptedOutcome:
      route: cheap
      decision: Small arithmetic fix with a focused unit test, so the cheap tier should finish it inside the small ceiling.
      attempts:
        - tier: cheap
          result: passed
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 15200, cachedInput: 2400, output: 730 }

  - id: T2
    title: Show customer name in the receipt email subject
    size: small
    issueNumber: 102
    description: |
      Receipt emails say "Your receipt is ready" for every customer. Include the
      customer display name in the subject while preserving the existing body
      template and fallback for missing names.
    passCheck: npm test -- --run tests/receipt-email.test.ts
    outcomes: [passed]
    scriptedOutcome:
      route: cheap
      decision: Template-only change with existing coverage, so the cheapest model is the right first attempt.
      attempts:
        - tier: cheap
          result: passed
          tokens: { uncachedInput: 11800, cachedInput: 2100, output: 520 }

  - id: T3
    title: Reject duplicate webhook deliveries by event id
    size: small
    issueNumber: 103
    description: |
      Payment webhooks can be delivered more than once. Add an idempotency guard
      keyed by the provider event id so duplicate deliveries do not create
      duplicate ledger entries.
    passCheck: npm test -- --run tests/webhook-idempotency.test.ts
    outcomes: [passed]
    scriptedOutcome:
      route: cheap
      decision: The affected code path is narrow and the test names the exact idempotency case, so start cheap.
      attempts:

  5) If `assets/` or templates exist, reuse them instead of recreating from scratch.

  - Announce which skill(s) you're using and why (one short line). If you skip an obvious skill, say why.

  - Progressive disclosure applies to selecting relevant files, not partially reading a selected instruction file. Do not load unrelated references, scripts, or assets.

  - When variants exist (frameworks, providers, domains), pick only the relevant reference file(s) and note that choice.

name: using-ao
description: "Catalog of the AO (Agent Orchestrator) `ao` CLI: spawning workers, managing sessions and projects, creating reusable Cues, sending messages, controlling the shared browser, previewing pages, and daemon control. Use when using the ao CLI, creating Cues, spawning workers, or managing AO sessions in an AO workspace."
trigger: "Using the ao CLI in an AO workspace: creating Cues, spawning workers, managing sessions/projects, sending messages, controlling or previewing pages."
---

# AO CLI Catalog

`ao` is a thin CLI over the local AO daemon. Every command is `ao <command> --help` for the authoritative flag list.

| Command | What it does | When to use | Details |
|---|---|---|---|
| `spawn` | Spawn a project worker, orchestrator, or projectless standalone worker | Starting a new task or issue | [commands/spawn.md](commands/spawn.md) |
| `session` | Manage agent sessions (list, kill, rename, restore, etc.) | Inspecting or controlling running/terminated sessions | [commands/session.md](commands/session.md) |
| `agent` | Inspect installed harnesses and launch readiness | Choosing or diagnosing an agent harness | `ao agent ls --refresh` |
| `pr` | Merge a PR or resolve its review threads | Completing a reviewed change | `ao pr merge` / `ao pr resolve-comments` |
| `project` | Register, inspect, configure, or remove projects | Setting up or managing repos AO knows about | [commands/project.md](commands/project.md) |
| `automation` | Manage durable recurring session automations | Creating, editing, disabling, deleting, and inspecting scheduled runs | [commands/automation.md](commands/automation.md) |
